name: mac-session-check-cache
title: Mac host: reuse a passing session and geometry check for 16 ms across capture and cursor verifies

commits: 3d1336b Reuse a passing Mac desktop check for 16 ms around capture and the pointer
43884e0 Time the Mac desktop check with and without reuse
5c35e3a Document the Mac desktop check reuse and record its measurement
impl.summary:
The branch starts from perf2/wave1 (bdbcd76). HEAD is detached at 5c35e3a and the working tree is clean.

- crates/pb-mapper-desktop/src/platform/mod.rs: the `Desktop` trait gains two provided methods, `prepare_recent(on_switch)` and `display_matches_recent(expected)`. By default they call `prepare` and `display_matches`, so Windows (`WinDesktop`), the unsupported platform and every other implementor behave exactly as before. The docs say a pass may be reused briefly (macOS: 16 ms), a failure never is, and `on_switch` does not run on a reuse.
- crates/pb-mapper-desktop/src/native.rs: `PlatformBackend::prepare(recent)` and `verify(expected, recent)`. capture_video (both checks) and cursor (both checks) pass `recent = true`. These stay fresh: `input_in_context` (the injection boundary), `set_display_mode`, stills, and `display()` / `context()` (the 100 ms context check). A new test, `only_capture_and_the_pointer_may_reuse_a_desktop_check`, runs on the synthetic platform and asserts which kind of check each path makes.
- crates/pb-mapper-desktop/src/platform/macos/reuse.rs (new): a pure `Reuse<G>` policy with the time passed in, `REUSE` = 16 ms. It is built and tested on every platform, like geometry.rs.
  - `session(now, recent, check)` reuses a pass taken within 16 ms.
  - `geometry(now, read)` is a fresh read that renews the reuse.
  - `matches(now, recent, read, fits)` reuses only a geometry that still fits; one that no longer fits is read again.
  - Any failure forgets both, and a clock that steps back reuses nothing.
  - Four unit tests cover call counts and the 16 ms edge, input always reading and renewing, failures never reused, and a geometry that no longer fits.
- crates/pb-mapper-desktop/src/platform/macos/mod.rs: registers `reuse` with the same pure-module pattern as the other macOS modules.
- crates/pb-mapper-desktop/src/platform/macos/desktop.rs: `MacDesktop` holds `Reuse<(CGDirectDisplayID, Geometry)>` and overrides `prepare_recent` and `display_matches_recent`. `prepare`, `display` and `display_matches` read fresh and renew the reuse. `read_geometry` becomes a free function so the closures borrow disjoint fields. `available` becomes `pub(super)` for the measurement test.
- crates/pb-mapper-desktop/src/platform/synthetic.rs: `SynDesktop` counts fresh and recent checks (`Checks`, `Probe::checks`) for the routing test.
- crates/pb-mapper-desktop/src/platform/macos/tests.rs: an ignored release measurement, `session_check_cost`, with back-to-back and paced arms. The paced arms run 60 FPS capture plus the pointer every 16 ms, with an idle baseline, and report wall time, thread CPU, WindowServer CPU via `ps`, and reads counted.
- Docs:
  - docs/remote-desktop.md: "inside each capture" now says the checks happen around each capture and pointer read, and the Mac reuse is described with a link to the measurements. The injection-boundary sentence is kept, and the macOS `Desktop` row of the platforms table is updated. There is no Chinese pair of this page.
  - New record docs/benchmarks/2026-11-24-mac-session-check/: README, six raw runs and the before variant's source. It is indexed in docs/README.md.
  - CHANGELOG.md: a bullet under [Unreleased].

No change to the wire protocol, helper protocol or ALPN.
impl.deviations:
1. Measurement: this Mac's screen was locked for the whole session, so `MacDesktop`'s session check failed ("the screen is locked"). Failures are never reused by design, so `MacDesktop`'s own recent path could not be timed in a passing state here.
   - When the check fails, the ignored test drives the same `Reuse` policy over the same WindowServer reads: `available()`, which reads the session dictionary and both keys whatever it answers, and `geometry(id)` plus the match. It takes the session's answer as a pass and counts each read.
   - It also times `MacDesktop`'s real recent checks while locked. Each of those read WindowServer, which shows on the real type that a failure is not reused.
   - On an unlocked Mac the same test times `MacDesktop` itself.
   - To make this possible, `available` became `pub(super)`.
2. "Before" binary: the base perf2/wave1 (bdbcd76) plus the same test with no reuse (every check makes both reads) and `available` made `pub(super)` for it. Its source is kept as before-variant.rs.txt. The before and after binaries ran alternately, three runs each.
3. Design choices beyond the brief:
   - A reused geometry that no longer matches the expected display is read again rather than reported as a mismatch, so reuse can only ever answer a pass.
   - Any failure, of the session check or of a geometry read, forgets both cached answers.
   - `set_display_mode` and stills also stay on fresh checks.
4. Known consequence of the 16 ms window, within the brief's accepted risk: right after a display mode change, the one pointer sample in the same worker iteration can pass on the pre-change geometry read moments before. The worker then re-checks the context immediately (`context_due = now`) before the next capture. Previously that sample would have failed and triggered a recovery.

impl.measurements:
Environment: release builds on a 12-core Apple M6 with 24 GiB, macOS 27.0 (26A425), Rust 1.99.1, main display 4096x2304. Other agents were building at the same time (load average 2.0-6.9). The screen was locked, so the checks ran through the `Reuse` policy over the real WindowServer reads (deviation 1). Figures are medians of 3 runs, with the range in brackets.

Back to back, 20,000 checks, µs per check:

| Checks | Wall | Thread CPU | WindowServer CPU | Reads per check |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Before | 51.5 (50.5-54.5) | 18.1 | 20.5 | 2 |
| After, fresh | 51.9 (51.3-57.4) | 18.2 | 20.5 | 2 |
| After, recent | 0.039 | 0.033 | 0 | 0 |
| `MacDesktop` recent while locked (session read only, never reused) | 37.2 | 12.0 | 11.5 | session only |

Paced, 10 s per arm, 245.0 checks/s in every arm:

| Arm | Checks that read WindowServer | Reads/s | Wall in checks (ms/s) | Thread CPU (ms/s) | WindowServer CPU (ms/s) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Before | 245 | 490 | 72.4 (68.0-81.9) | 25.9 (20.4-30.8) | 38 (36-70) |
| After, fresh | 245 | 490 | 74.8 | 27.8 (13.1-29.4) | 36 (33-40) |
| After, recent | 61.3 (60.6-61.6) | 119.8 | 24.4 (23.2-24.9) | 8.8 (8.6-9.9) | 17 (16-18) |

Idle arms: thread CPU about 1.2 ms/s for the pacing loop; WindowServer 5-9 ms/s, except one before run at 34. Paced, a check that reads costs the thread about 100 µs of CPU, against 18 µs back to back.
impl.device_only:
- `session_check_cost` on an unlocked Mac, where it times `MacDesktop`'s own fresh and recent checks.
- On a Mac host during `target/release/examples/deployed APP_CONFIG_PATH OUT/<arm>-<n> selftest 40 --tcp`, view-only and with the pointer moving, before and after:

- That a lock or a fast user switch stops capture and the pointer within 16 ms while input stays refused at once. This needs a person at the Mac.

findings.issue: A display mode change made by this backend leaves its own pre-change pass in the reuse cache. `set_display_mode` calls `verify(expected, false)`, and that fresh read stores the pre-change geometry in `MacDesktop.reuse`, stamped microseconds before `self.modes.set(...)` changes the mode. `restore_display_mode` never clears the cache either. For the next 16 ms a recent check against the old context answers from the geometry that no longer exists. Before this PR, that check read WindowServer and failed. The guide says to key a cache on exactly the inputs that change the result, and this backend's own mode change is one of those inputs. The cache does not see it.
findings.evidence:
Path traced in worker.rs `iterate`:
1. The second `drain_slot_lane` loop runs after `capture_step`.
2. A `LaneCommand::DisplayMode` there calls `display_mode` -> `backend.set_display_mode` (verify false: `Reuse::geometry` stores (id, G_old) at t) -> `modes.set`. `mode_changed` then only sets `context_due = now`.
3. `self.sample_cursor(now)` runs in the same iteration. `cursor()` calls `verify(expected, true)`. `Reuse::session` reuses the pass from t. `Reuse::matches` finds G_old inside the 16 ms window, and `fits` against the old `expected.display`, so it returns `Ok(true)` without reading.
4. `MacCursor::read` then converts with `self.geometry.get()`, the shared Cell that still holds G_old (cursor.rs:217,228). It reports a pointer in the old context instead of failing with 'desktop changed before cursor capture' as the base did.
The implementer reports this as deviation 4. Capture is not affected, because `capture_step` checks the context first when `context_due = now`.
findings.fix: Make a mode change drop what capture and the pointer reuse. Add a provided `fn forget_recent(&mut self) {}` to `Desktop`, and have `MacDesktop` override it with `self.reuse = Reuse::default()`. Call it from `PlatformBackend::set_display_mode` after `self.modes.set(..)`, and from `restore_display_mode`'s `on change` closure or after it returns `Ok(true)`. The next recent check then reads, as before this PR. Extend `only_capture_and_the_pointer_may_reuse_a_desktop_check`, or add a `reuse.rs` case, so that a recent check after a mode change reads.

findings.issue: The CHANGELOG bullet presents its figures as a Mac sharing its screen: 61 of 245 checks, thread CPU 8.8 vs 25.9 ms/s, WindowServer 17 vs 38 ms/s. None of them came from `MacDesktop` in a passing state. The screen was locked for every run. The figures come from the test's stand-in, which drives the `Reuse` policy over `available()` and `geometry(id)` and takes the failed session answer as a pass. WindowServer's CPU was also measured with the lock screen up. The benchmark README discloses all of this. The CHANGELOG and the docs/remote-desktop.md paragraph (around line 1419, '61 of the 245 checks a second read WindowServer') do not.
findings.evidence: docs/benchmarks/2026-11-24-mac-session-check/README.md: 'The screen of this Mac was locked throughout ... On an unlocked Mac the test times `MacDesktop`'s checks instead; that run is still to be made.' Every raw file prints 'the session check fails here: the screen is locked' and 'verifies=reads_as_passing'. My own release run of `session_check_cost` here also reported the screen locked, with 62.2 reads/s and 7.0 ms/s of thread CPU in the paced recent arm.
findings.fix: In the CHANGELOG bullet and the remote-desktop.md paragraph, qualify the numbers, for example: 'measured through the same reads and reuse policy with this Mac's screen locked; a run on an unlocked host is still to be made'. Alternatively, keep only the read count (61 of 245, which the policy and the pacing fix) and leave the CPU figures to the linked README.

reviews.notes:
Verdict: ready. Neither finding blocks merging. I read every changed line of `perf2/wave1..perf2/mac-session-check-cache` and the code around it. That covered `worker.rs` iterate order, `worker/modes.rs`, `worker/capture.rs`, `worker/cursor.rs`, `backend.rs` capture_checked, the macOS cursor's use of the shared geometry, and `WinDesktop`.

**Checked and correct:**
- Routing:
  - Capture and cursor checks pass `recent = true`.
  - `input_in_context`, `set_display_mode`, stills and `display()`/`context()` stay fresh, so the injection boundary and the 100 ms context check still read WindowServer.
  - Windows, the unsupported platform and every other implementor get the provided defaults and behave exactly as before.
- The `Desktop` trait additions are provided methods, and no `impl Desktop` carries `#[deny(clippy::missing_trait_methods)]` (only the Backend impls do). They compile for Windows by construction.
- `Reuse` policy:
  - A failure is never cached, and any failure, session or geometry, forgets both.
  - The window is `age < 16 ms`, measured from before the read.
  - A backwards clock reuses nothing (`checked_duration_since`).
  - Only a geometry that still fits is reused, and a stale display id is re-read every time until the context recovers.
  - The shared `Rc<Cell<Geometry>>` always equals the cached geometry, because both change only in `read_geometry`.
- `on_switch` still runs on every failure.
- The synthetic platform is `#[cfg(test)]`, and the `reuse` module is dead-code-allowed off macOS.
- No wire, helper-protocol or ALPN change, and nothing is added per packet.

**Run here (Apple M6, macOS 27.0, Rust 1.99.1):**
- The 5 new tests pass.
- `cargo test -p pb-mapper-desktop --all-features --lib`: 217 passed, 22 ignored.
- `cargo clippy -p pb-mapper-desktop --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: clean.
- `RUSTDOCFLAGS=-D warnings cargo doc -p pb-mapper-desktop --no-deps`: clean.
- One release run of `session_check_cost`. The screen was still locked, and the paced recent arm matched the record: 62.2 reads/s, 7.0 ms/s of thread CPU, against 25.6 ms/s for the fresh arm.

**Not run here:** Windows and Linux CI, nat-traversal, and `MacDesktop`'s own path with the screen unlocked.

Build output was removed with `rm -rf target ui/build`, and the worktree at `/Users/lb7666/rust_pro/pb-mapper/.claude/worktrees/wf_352d1379-280-10` is clean and detached at 5c35e3a.

findings.issue: No test that runs anywhere covers how MacDesktop maps the trait methods onto the reuse policy: `prepare` and `display_matches` read fresh, `prepare_recent` and `display_matches_recent` may reuse. If either fresh method passed `recent = true`, every input on a Mac would accept a pass up to 16 ms old. That breaks the documented rule that the injection boundary re-checks for every input, and the whole suite stays green. The policy tests (reuse.rs) and the routing test (native.rs, on the synthetic platform) both pass, but neither reaches MacDesktop. The ignored measurement, the only code that calls MacDesktop's checks, could not run MacDesktop's reuse in a passing state here because the screen was locked. So no run anywhere has confirmed that MacDesktop's mapping reads fresh for input and reuses for capture and the pointer.
findings.evidence: Mutation run here: in desktop.rs I changed `fn prepare` to `self.session(true, on_switch)` and `fn display_matches` to `self.matches(expected, true)`. Then `cargo test -p pb-mapper-desktop --all-features` reported lib 217 passed, 22 ignored, and every other target passed. I restored the file afterwards. By contrast, the routing mutation (`input_in_context` passing `true`) and the edge mutation (`age <= REUSE`) each fail a new test.
findings.fix: Count MacDesktop's WindowServer reads under `#[cfg(test)]`: a counter field incremented in `session`'s check closure and in the `read_geometry` closures. Add a non-ignored test in platform/macos/tests.rs that opens the main display. It should check: `display()` then `display_matches_recent` makes 0 geometry reads; `display_matches` makes 1 each time. If `prepare` passes, `prepare` twice reads twice and a following `prepare_recent` reads 0; if the session check fails (locked screen), report and skip only that half. The geometry half runs with a locked screen too. Avoid a fn-pointer seam: thread C's checks must stay static.

findings.issue: The bullet presents its figures as a Mac host's measured effect without saying where they came from. They come from a paced test loop on a Mac whose screen was locked, which drove the `Reuse` policy over the raw WindowServer reads with the session answer taken as a pass. MacDesktop's own passing path and a live host were never timed. The README says so; the CHANGELOG does not. "The checking thread" is the test thread, not thread C. The bullet's opening, "about a quarter as often while it captures", generalises the moving-picture 60 FPS case. On a still screen the Mac source submits only at its liveness or keyframe deadline (video.rs `idle_until`), so mostly the pointer's checks run, and samples at least 16 ms apart leave only the second check of each sample reusable. That ratio was not measured.
findings.evidence: README: "The screen of this Mac was locked throughout ... The test therefore made the same reads ... through the same `Reuse` policy, taking the session's answer as a pass ... On an unlocked Mac the test times `MacDesktop`'s checks instead; that run is still to be made." Raw files: every run prints `verifies=reads_as_passing`. My own release run here was also locked and gave paced recent=true over_10us_per_s=61.3. Its WindowServer CPU was 38 ms/s against 77 for the fresh arm, with 21 idle, so the WindowServer figure is noisy on a shared machine. platform/macos/video.rs `idle_until` returns `last_submit + LIVENESS_INTERVAL` for a Repeatable (still) stream.
findings.fix: Qualify the bullet. Drop "about a quarter as often while it captures", or limit it to a moving picture at 60 FPS. Say the figures come from a 60 FPS paced loop of the same WindowServer reads, measured with the screen locked, and replace "the checking thread" with "the checking loop". Keep the 61-of-245 count, which depends only on the policy and the pacing. Add no unmeasured still-screen figure.

reviews.notes:
Lens: effect and completeness. Branch perf2/mac-session-check-cache (5c35e3a) against perf2/wave1 (bdbcd76). I read every changed line plus the worker paths that call it: worker/capture.rs, worker/cursor.rs, worker/modes.rs, the worker loop, and macos/video.rs.

**Brief coverage**
1. Desktop trait: provided `prepare_recent` and `display_matches_recent` that default to `prepare` and `display_matches`. Done. WinDesktop, unsupported and the helper keep the defaults, so their behaviour does not change.
2. native.rs `verify(expected, recent)`: both capture_video checks and both cursor checks pass true. `input_in_context`, `set_display_mode`, stills, `display()` and `context()` stay fresh. Done.
3. Pure `Reuse<G>` with the time passed in, built on every platform. It reuses while `age < 16 ms` and never renews a pass when reusing one. Any failure forgets both cached answers; a clock that steps back reuses nothing. Fresh `prepare`, `display` and `display_matches` renew it. Done.
   - Beyond the brief: a cached geometry that no longer matches is read again, so a reuse can only ever answer a pass. This is sound.
   - `on_switch` runs only on a failure, as before.
4. Tests: four policy tests and the synthetic routing test. I mutated three things here: input routed as recent, `<=` at the 16 ms edge, and the window renewed on reuse. Each fails a test.
5. Docs: the host paragraph now says "around each capture and pointer read", correct for Windows too, and describes the Mac reuse; the injection-boundary sentence is kept. The macOS row of the platforms table is updated.
   - remote-desktop.md has no Chinese pair.
   - The benchmark record is indexed in docs/README.md, and the CHANGELOG bullet is under [Unreleased].
- No wire, helper-protocol or ALPN change. No error types, environment writes, thiserror or anyhow. Lint and dead_code conventions match the sibling pure modules.

**Measurement honesty**
- Every median and range in the README and CHANGELOG matches the six raw files; I recomputed each.
- The environment (M6, 24 GiB, macOS 27.0, Rust 1.99.1, load averages) is recorded. The before variant's source is kept, and the locked-screen proxy is disclosed in the README.
- My own release run of `session_check_cost` (screen still locked) reproduced 61.3 reading checks a second and about 119.5 reads a second.
- Small nit, not filed: README line 90 says "as the thread wakes for each tick" as a cause. The idle arm wakes on the same ticks and costs about 1.2 ms/s, so that cause is not what the data shows.

**Effect**
- In the worker, cursor samples are at least 16 ms apart (`cursor_due = now + 16 ms`) and capture runs at 60 Hz. So on a moving picture reads fall to about one check per 16 ms, as the paced model shows.
- On a still screen the Mac source rarely submits, so mostly the pointer's checks run and the saving is smaller. This is not measured; it is the reason for the CHANGELOG finding.
- The accepted risk holds: a lock, or an external mode change, reaches capture and the pointer up to 16 ms later, and input stays fresh.
- The implementer's deviation 4: after pb-mapper's own mode change in the post-capture drain, one pointer sample may pass on the geometry read just before the change. The next iteration's context check (`context_due = now`) corrects it. Harmless, since viewers still show the old picture. A provided `Desktop::forget_recent()` called after `modes.set` and restore would remove it if wanted; I did not file it.

**Run here**
- `cargo test -p pb-mapper-desktop --all-features --lib`: 217 passed, 22 ignored. The 5 new tests pass.
- `cargo clippy -p pb-mapper-desktop --all-targets --all-features -D warnings`: clean.
- The release ignored measurement ran once (results above).
- Mutations were applied and reverted; the tree is clean.

**Not run here**
- Windows and Linux CI (the trait change only adds provided methods), and nat-traversal.
- `session_check_cost` on an unlocked Mac, which is the only thing that would time MacDesktop's own reuse path.
- A live-host `sample` and `top` run.

00359e6 Say the Mac desktop check figures come from a locked-screen stand-in
fixed: Reviewer 1, native.rs: a mode change left a stale geometry in the reuse cache. I confirmed it by tracing the worker. In iterate, the post-capture drain_slot_lane runs set_display_mode. That call's fresh verify stores the pre-change geometry in MacDesktop.reuse. sample_cursor then runs in the same iteration, and its recent verify reused that geometry within 16 ms. The fix: platform/mod.rs gives Desktop a provided `fn forget_recent(&mut self) {}`, and MacDesktop overrides it with `self.reuse.forget()` (`Reuse::forget` is now pub(crate)). PlatformBackend::set_display_mode calls it after `modes.set`, and restore_display_mode after `modes.restore`, whatever the result. WinDesktop and the unsupported platform keep the no-op default. Tests: SynDesktop counts forgets (Checks.forgets), and only_capture_and_the_pointer_may_reuse_a_desktop_check now asserts a forget after a set and after a restore. reuse.rs adds a_forget_leaves_nothing_to_reuse.

Reviewer 2, macos/desktop.rs: no test covered how MacDesktop maps the trait methods onto the reuse policy. MacDesktop now counts its WindowServer reads in a Reads type, which has fields only under cfg(test) and is zero-sized otherwise. A new non-ignored macOS test, only_capture_and_the_pointer_reuse_a_mac_desktop_check, opens the main display and checks the geometry: display_matches and display read every time, display_matches_recent reuses after display, and a forget makes the next check read. For the session it checks the same three things while the check passes; while it fails (locked screen) it checks that each prepare_recent reads and runs on_switch. A round that takes 16 ms or longer is rerun, up to 5 times. It skips on a runner with no display. Mutations, each reverted: display_matches made recent fails it; forget_recent made a no-op fails it; dropping the forget in set_display_mode fails the native test.

Both reviewers, CHANGELOG.md: the figures were presented as a Mac sharing its screen. The bullet now says they come from a test loop on an M6 Mac that made the same reads through the same reuse, paced as a moving picture at 60 FPS. It says the screen was locked, so the loop stood in for the real check, and that a run on an unlocked Mac and in a live session is still to be made. It keeps the 61 of 245 count and the loop's 8.8 vs 25.9 ms/s, drops the WindowServer figure and the 'about a quarter as often' line, and says a resolution change or restore leaves nothing to reuse.

docs/remote-desktop.md: the paragraph now calls the 61 of 245 figure a locked-screen stand-in loop and says a run on an unlocked Mac is still to be made. It describes the mode-change forget and says which events (a lock, another login, a display changed from outside the session) reach capture and the pointer up to 16 ms later. The macOS row of the platforms table mentions the forget.

docs/benchmarks/2026-11-24-mac-session-check/README.md: notes that WindowServer CPU was measured with the lock screen up and is too noisy to read as more than a direction. impl.summary:
The branch is perf2/mac-wake-display, based on perf2/mac-session-check-cache (00359e6). The worktree is detached and target is deleted.

Code, under crates/pb-mapper-desktop/src/platform/macos/:

- wake.rs (new, pure, built and tested on every platform like reuse.rs):
  - WAKE_EVERY = 2 s.
  - WakeLimiter (const new; admit(now) allows at most one declaration per 2 s; settled(now) says whether the last one is at least 2 s old).
  - wakeable(asleep, builtin, lid_closed): a display is woken if it sleeps, except the built-in panel when the lid is closed. The lid is read only for a sleeping built-in panel.
  - Two tests: one covers the limiter against capture's 200 ms retries, the other the closed-lid rule.
- power.rs (new, macOS only):
  - IOKit externs linked with #[link(name = "IOKit", kind = "framework")]: IOPMAssertionDeclareUserActivity, IOPMAssertionRelease, IOServiceMatching, IOServiceGetMatchingService, IORegistryEntryCreateCFProperty, IOObjectRelease. Signatures were checked against the macOS 27 SDK headers.
  - A static parking_lot Mutex holds the WakeLimiter and the IOPMAssertionID, which is passed back on each declaration as the header asks.
  - wake(ids) -> bool: declares kIOPMUserActiveLocal (rate-limited) when any of the ids sleeps and can be woken, and returns whether one does.
  - wake_for_session(display): if desktop::available() passes and an online display (CGGetOnlineDisplayList) sleeps, it wakes them, then checks every 100 ms, for up to 2 s, until the shared display is active and awake. The display is matched by UUID, or by id when it has no name.
  - release(): frees the assertion id once the declaration is at least 2 s old.
  - Also online(), drawing(display), lid_closed() (AppleClamshellState on IOPMrootDomain, with the service released after the read), and waking(), a CaptureFailed error "the display is asleep; waking it".
  - Log events: desktop_display_wake (debug) and desktop_display_wake_failed (warn, with the IOReturn).
- mod.rs: registers wake as pure and power as macOS-only. Macos::open calls power::wake_for_session(display) before MacDesktop::open (call site a).
- video.rs: MacVideo stores the display id and a `resumed` flag.
  - (b) MacVideo::open wakes a sleeping display and fails with waking(). This also covers recoveries.
  - (c) A DisplayLost from Stream::start while the display sleeps, or the 3 s no-picture failure while it sleeps, also becomes waking().
  - Resume: a new VideoSource::paused override sets `resumed`. The next submit, which runs after the backend's session check, wakes a sleeping display and fails, so capture reopens through (b). idle_until returns None while a resume is pending.
- timer.rs: when the last guard is released, it ends the activity and then calls power::release().
- tests.rs: a new macOS test, a_woken_display_is_found_by_the_name_it_is_bound_by. It checks that every active display is online, that an awake display is found by its UUID and by its id, that another UUID is not, and that the lid read works. Nothing is woken.

Docs:
- docs/remote-desktop.md: the "Sharing a Mac" bullet; the macOS host paragraph, linking a new section "Waking a sleeping Mac display"; the pure-parts sentence and the file tree; a new row in the acceptance table.
- docs/architecture.md: the timer.rs line and the platform/macos list.
- docs/user-guide.md and docs/user-guide.zh-CN.md, changed together: a sleeping Mac display comes back on when a viewer connects or resumes, except on a locked Mac; with the lid closed, only an external display.
- CHANGELOG.md: one bullet under [Unreleased].

No protocol, wire, helper or HELPER_PROTOCOL change.
impl.deviations:
1. Resume: the brief says "(b) also covers a resume, whose capture reopens here". On this base it does not. MacVideo had no `paused` override, so the stream stays open across a pause and a resume replays the old picture. To get the brief's intent, MacVideo now implements VideoSource::paused. The first submit after a resume, which runs after the backend's session check, wakes a sleeping display and fails with "the display is asleep; waking it". The backend then drops the source, and thread C's retry reopens it through (b).

2. (b) stops early instead of starting the stream: when the display sleeps and can be woken, MacVideo::open declares activity and fails with CaptureFailed before it builds the encoder or the stream, as airhand's SckCapturer::open does. The brief only asked to call wake before Stream::start. Starting a ScreenCaptureKit stream on a sleeping display would cost the 3 s no-picture wait or a 200 ms DisplayLost loop of display enumerations.

3. The start-of-session wait (a) is 2 s, not 3 s. Macos::open runs inside the backend factory, before describe(), and the acceptor gives the whole factory plus describe BACKEND_ANSWER_WAIT (3 s). A 3 s wait would push a slow-waking session to fallback caps (no H.265, no display modes). A const assert ties WAKE_WAIT + 500 ms to BACKEND_ANSWER_WAIT. A display slower than 2 s is still caught by (b)'s retry.

4. The assertion is released only when it is at least 2 s old. Thread C releases the timer guard in the same step that a no-picture failure (c) declares activity, so releasing unconditionally would free the assertion microseconds after the declaration. A younger assertion is left to powerd's own timeout and reused by the next declaration.

5. The pure rules are in a separate file, wake.rs (WakeLimiter and the lid rule), built everywhere like reuse.rs. power.rs is macOS-only because it links IOKit.

6. wake(ids) returns whether any of the ids sleeps and can be woken, not just whether one sleeps. So the built-in panel behind a closed lid keeps the old "delivered no picture" failure instead of saying "waking it".

Out of scope, not done: a read-only probe on this Mac (python ctypes, `cgprobe.py` in the scratchpad) found its sleeping external display online, asleep and inactive, with bounds 2048x1152 and a mode still readable, and CGMainDisplayID returning it. So MacDesktop::open and the context check work by id while the display sleeps. But `support()` uses desktop::any_display(), which reads the active list, so a host started or relaunched while every display sleeps reports no_display. That host-start case is not covered by this PR and could be a follow-up.

findings.issue: Only the H.264/H.265 path wakes a sleeping display on resume or when capture fails. A JPEG session does not, so the docs overstate what the PR does. When codec == Jpeg, capture_video returns through capture_consistent -> still -> SckStill::jpeg and never opens a MacVideo. self.video stays None, so video_paused(false) changes nothing, MacVideo::paused/submit never runs, and still.rs has no wake. The JPEG path gets only call site (a), at session start. A JPEG viewer (the documented fallback, for example a Linux viewer without the GStreamer packages) that pauses lets the activity go (capturing is false while paused, so the timer guard drops and the display may sleep). When it resumes, its screenshots of the sleeping display fail or come back dark until someone touches the Mac. The user guide (EN and zh-CN), the CHANGELOG and remote-desktop.md all say a sleeping display comes back on 'when a viewer connects or resumes', with no codec exception.
findings.evidence: native.rs:206-219: `if codec == VideoCodec::Jpeg { return Ok(Some(EncodedFrame { ..., bytes: self.capture_consistent(expected)? })) }` returns before `P::Video::open`. native.rs video_paused: `if let Some((_, video)) = &mut self.video { video.paused(paused) }`, a no-op without a source. platform/macos/still.rs:48-56: `screenshot` goes straight to `self.filter(display.id)?` (capture::display, the SCK enumeration) with no power:: call. worker.rs:875: `capturing = !self.paused && ...` drops the TimerResolution guard while paused. docs/user-guide.md:464: 'A Mac display that has gone to sleep comes back on when a viewer connects or resumes'.
findings.fix: In platform/macos/still.rs SckStill::screenshot, map a failed filter or screenshot, while `power::wake([display.id])` is true, to `power::waking()`. That is the same treatment as call site (c), and it costs nothing when the screenshot succeeds. PlatformBackend::still runs `prepare(false)` (the session check) just before, so a locked Mac still stays dark. Alternatively, make the docs and CHANGELOG say the resume and no-picture wakes apply to H.264/H.265 sessions.

Verdict: ready. I found one minor issue: a JPEG session is not woken on resume or capture failure, though the docs say it is.

I read the whole diff of perf2/mac-session-check-cache..perf2/mac-wake-display (3ca0dcc, 46418fd) and the code around it: worker/capture.rs (capture_step, fail, capture_at, deadline), worker.rs (the TimerResolution hold), native.rs (verify, capture_video, video_paused), platform/mod.rs (VideoSource), macos desktop.rs, capture.rs, still.rs, timer.rs, host/acceptor.rs and worker::prepare.

What I checked and found correct:
- **IOKit signatures:** checked against the macOS SDK headers. IOPMAssertionDeclareUserActivity(CFStringRef, IOPMUserActiveType, IOPMAssertionID*) matches, with kIOPMUserActiveLocal=0 and kIOPMNullAssertionID=0. IOServiceMatching returns retained (CF_RETURNS_RETAINED) and IOServiceGetMatchingService consumes it (CF_RELEASES_ARGUMENT). IORegistryEntryCreateCFProperty follows the Create rule and is wrapped in CFRetained::from_raw. IOObjectRelease runs once.
- **objc2-core-graphics 0.3.2:** CGDisplayIsAsleep and CGDisplayIsBuiltin are safe fns; CGGetOnlineDisplayList is unsafe, with pointers to local storage.
- **Locks:** WOKEN is taken inside timer::HELD and never the other way round, so there is no deadlock. Calls from several rooms are serialized correctly by the WOKEN lock.
- **The resume path cannot spin:**
  - idle_until returns None only until the first submit, which takes `resumed`.
  - deadline() uses context_due while capture is unavailable.
  - A blocked tick still consumes the pacer.
- **Session check before every wake:**
  - (a) calls desktop::available() itself.
  - (b), (c) and resume run in capture_video after verify(expected, true): prepare_recent, reused for at most 16 ms.
- **The 2 s wait:** it runs inside the spawn_blocking factory, and the const assert keeps WAKE_WAIT + 500 ms within BACKEND_ANSWER_WAIT.
- **No per-frame cost:** only an open, the first submit after a resume and the failure path touch power::.
- **Compatibility:** no wire, capability, ALPN or HELPER_PROTOCOL change. The pure wake.rs is cfg-allowed for dead code off macOS; tests.rs and power.rs are macOS-only, and IOKit is cfg(macos), so iOS is untouched.
- **Docs and CHANGELOG:** the EN and zh-CN user-guide edits change together, and the CHANGELOG contains no unmeasured figures.

findings.issue: Viewers that get JPEG stills (no hardware decoder, for example a Linux viewer without the GStreamer packages) are only covered when the session starts. If the display sleeps during a pause, nothing wakes it when they resume, and nothing wakes it when ScreenCaptureKit does not list it. Yet CHANGELOG.md:7 and the user-guide pair say a sleeping Mac display comes back on when a viewer connects or resumes.
findings.evidence: For JPEG, PlatformBackend::capture_video calls capture_consistent, then still(), then SckStill::jpeg/screenshot, which calls self.filter(display.id) and then capture::display(id). It never calls power::wake. PlatformBackend::video_paused (native.rs:377-381) only forwards to an open video source, and a JPEG session has none, so the new MacVideo::paused/resumed path never runs for it. The brief's step (c) names "a DisplayLost from capture::display" in general, and SckStill::filter is the other caller of capture::display. On resume, a still of a sleeping display therefore fails (or returns no picture) every 200 ms, and no declaration is made. With no presented frame, the viewer's input is not admitted either.
findings.fix: In SckStill::screenshot, before self.filter(display.id), add `if power::wake([display.id]) { return Err(power::waking()); }`. PlatformBackend::still has already run prepare(false), so the session check passed. Map a DisplayLost from self.filter the same way as in MacVideo::open. Or narrow the CHANGELOG and user-guide wording to video sessions.

findings.issue: Step (c) only fires when a stream never delivered its first picture. A display that sleeps while a stream is open, after its first picture (the owner puts it to sleep while unlocked, for example with a hot corner or pmset displaysleepnow), keeps the viewer on the last picture, repeated, and nothing wakes it. CHANGELOG.md:7 ('or when capture gets no picture from it') and docs/remote-desktop.md:1571 ('an open capture got no picture for 3 s') read as if that case were covered. airhand covers it: its SckCapturer::next checks CGDisplayIsAsleep every STATE_CHECK during an open stream and fails with 'the display went to sleep', which reopens and wakes.
findings.evidence: In video.rs::submit, the wake on the no-picture path runs only when `self.last_submit.is_none() && now >= self.created + FIRST_SUBMIT_WAIT`. Once a picture was submitted, `repeat` is true every LIVENESS_INTERVAL, and Stream::take(repeat) returns latest.picture, the old one, so submit keeps returning Ok(true) on a stale picture. Nothing in MacVideo checks CGDisplayIsAsleep again while the stream is open. Compare airhand client/src-tauri/src/host/capture/sck.rs: `if CGDisplayIsAsleep(self.display.id) { bail!("the display went to sleep"); }` inside next(). A view-only viewer cannot wake the display, and its picture stays frozen. A controlling viewer may still wake it through injected input.
findings.fix: In submit, when the take has no fresh arrival and the last fresh picture is at least about 1 s old, check `power::wake([self.display])`, at most once a second as airhand's STATE_CHECK does, and fail with power::waking() so that thread C reopens through (b). Or limit the CHANGELOG and docs wording to a capture that never got its first picture.

fixed: JPEG sessions (both reviewers): confirmed. A JPEG capture goes capture_consistent -> still -> SckStill::screenshot and never opens a MacVideo, so neither the resume nor the no-picture wake ran for it. SckStill::screenshot (crates/pb-mapper-desktop/src/platform/macos/still.rs) now looks before every screenshot, after PlatformBackend::still's prepare(false) session check: a sleeping display fails the still with power::waking() and is lit. Looking first also covers a screenshot that would succeed with a black picture. Each look is one CGDisplayIsAsleep read while the display is awake; stills run at up to 8 FPS.

Display put to sleep under an open stream after its first picture (reviewer 2): confirmed. Stream::take(repeat) keeps returning the old picture, and nothing looked at CGDisplayIsAsleep again. MacVideo::submit (video.rs) now looks at a repeat with no new picture, at most every ASLEEP_LOOK = 500 ms, as airhand's STATE_CHECK does. A display found asleep is lit and the submit fails with waking(), so thread C reopens the stream through call site (b). A const assert ties ASLEEP_LOOK + LIVENESS_INTERVAL < SETTLE. One correction to the reviewer: repeats are produced frames, so a controlling viewer's input was still admitted. A view-only viewer, though, stayed frozen.

Lock race added by the new mid-capture checks (found while fixing): when macOS asks for the password as soon as the display turns off, a display just found asleep may be turning off as the Mac locks. Lighting it at once would turn on the lock screen and break the documented rule that a locked Mac stays dark. A new pure wake::SleepWatch handles this. A display found asleep with nothing found in the second before it (a session's start, a resume) is lit at once. One found asleep within SETTLE = 1 s of being found awake (a new picture, a look or a still) is lit only after it has been found asleep for 1 s, with each look after a session check. Until then the stream repeats its last picture and a still fails. The new test a_display_that_turns_off_under_capture_is_left_dark_for_a_second covers it. Mutating any of the five rule expressions makes a wake.rs test fail.
wake_for_session could wait up to 2.1 s (reviewer 2's note): each sleep is now capped at the time left, so the wait never passes WAKE_WAIT, which the const assert against BACKEND_ANSWER_WAIT counts.

Smaller changes: power.rs now has sleeping(id) and light() alongside wake(ids). wakeable() takes the built-in flag lazily, so an awake display costs one Core Graphics read instead of two. The macOS identity test also asserts that an active, awake display is not taken as sleeping.

Docs updated: the remote-desktop.md 'Sharing a Mac' bullet, the macOS host paragraph, the 'Waking a sleeping Mac display' section (new stream and still bullets, plus the 1 s rule stated as a design rule, with how fast macOS reports the lock marked as still to try on a device) and the acceptance row; architecture.md's wake.rs line; the CHANGELOG bullet (now H.264/H.265 and JPEG, and a display turned off during a session); and the user-guide.md / user-guide.zh-CN.md pair, changed together. Follow-up: a host started while every display sleeps reports NoDisplay (support() and name resolution read the active display list).

impl.summary:
All work is on branch perf2/mac-vt-submit-thread, built on perf2/mac-wake-display (5491036). The worktree is left detached at 0280a23 and its target/ build output is deleted.

crates/pb-mapper-desktop/src/platform/macos/encoder.rs
- Encoder::build starts one std::thread named "pb-mapper-vt-submit" after prepare_to_encode_frames. The encodes() probe gets no thread.
- serve() makes every call on the VideoToolbox session, one at a time, inside objc2 autoreleasepool, and holds no lock during a call. That covers EncodeFrame with ForceKeyFrame, AverageBitRate with DataRateLimits (apply()) and the final invalidate.
- The thread owns a SendSession: a session clone plus the ForceKeyFrame dictionary, marked Send with a SAFETY note. A Job (a CFRetained picture, pts, keyframe, token) is also marked Send.
- State gains a one-slot mailbox under the existing mutex: job, rate (latest wins), in_call, c_waiting, stop and exited, plus a parking_lot Condvar in Shared.
- encode() pushes Pending with at=now exactly as before (dwell, late() and the OUTPUT_WAIT stall check are unchanged), places the Job, notifies and returns.
- A non-zero status, or an AverageBitRate refusal, removes the matching Pending, sets state.failure and wakes thread C. drain() reports it through codec_error, so H.265 still ends with EncoderFailed.
- After each call the thread clears in_call. If c_waiting is set, it clears it and wakes thread C.
- set_bitrate() now only stores the rate and notifies the thread, and returns ().
- New admit(limit) returns Full when in_flight (pending.len()) >= limit, which counts gate_ticks. Otherwise it returns Busy when a job waits or a call is under way, which sets c_waiting and counts armed_refusals. Otherwise Free.
- New waiting() reports c_waiting.
- Drop sets stop and waits on the Condvar until `exited` or LATE_OUTPUT, then joins. If the deadline passes, it detaches the thread and warns macos_encoder_left_running; the thread still holds Arc<Shared> and the session.
- Load traces `macos_encoder_load` at debug on pb_mapper_desktop::feedback: seconds, call_p50_us, call_p99_us, units, gate_ticks, armed_refusals, peak_in_flight. It uses a fixed 256-entry array and allocates nothing.
- Test-only helpers: hold, tear_down, in_call, idle, alive, average_bitrate, plus a session field.

crates/pb-mapper-desktop/src/platform/macos/video.rs
- New `pub(super) const VT_IN_FLIGHT: usize = 2`, documented with the measured figures, and `const _: () = assert!(VT_IN_FLIGHT + 1 < ENCODER_DEPTH)`.
- MacVideo::submit calls admit(VT_IN_FLIGHT) before taking a picture: Full returns Ok(true), which spends the tick; Busy returns Ok(false), which keeps the tick armed and keeps self.keyframe.
- idle_until returns now + LATE_OUTPUT while waiting(), so thread C does not spin.
- set_rate no longer fails on the encoder.
- The Phase 0 trace `macos_capture_layout` (debug, session target) is logged at the first picture. It reports CVPixelBufferGetExtendedPixels, the rows and bytes per row of both planes, and IOSurfaceGetAllocSize (through extern declarations, so no new dependency).
- The worker's generic gate, QUEUE_DEPTH and Windows' MAX_IN_FLIGHT are unchanged.

crates/pb-mapper-desktop/src/platform/macos/tests.rs
- New tests:

  - an_encoder_dropped_mid_encode_neither_hangs_nor_calls_back (a picture held in the mailbox, and a call in progress at 1920x1088)

Docs
- docs/remote-desktop.md: pipeline rule 2; the encoder-gate paragraph (two units for VideoToolbox, and why, with figures); the macOS hosting paragraph (submit thread, armed ticks, bitrate handling, drop); the input_wait paragraph; the new ignored tests; the diagnostics macos_encoder_load, macos_capture_layout and macos_encoder_left_running; and empty_polls_per_s now noting busy refusals.

impl.deviations:
1. in_flight() counts only state.pending.len(). encode() queues the job's Pending at hand-off, as the design requires, so adding the mailbox job again would count it twice. For the same reason pending() keeps its old formula (in-session + ready + failure); the mailbox's unit is already in it.

2. idle_until checks Encoder::waiting(), which is true only after a submit has been refused, not whether the thread is busy. A refusal is counted once per busy spell, so armed_refusals equals due ticks refused. mac-vt-rate-control's H.265 rule needs that count; with busy() in idle_until, thread C would never call submit while the thread was busy, and armed_refusals would stay near zero. The cost is one cheap capture_video call per busy spell, which desktop_capture_pacing counts as an empty poll (now documented).

3. Encoder::encode returns a plain error (not a codec failure) if a picture already waits in the mailbox, rather than queuing or replacing it. MacVideo always calls admit() first, so it cannot reach this.

4. Job carries no `duplicate`; the matching Pending already holds it.

5. QoS: a probe showed that a new pthread on macOS takes QOS_CLASS_DEFAULT (0x15) whatever its creator's class (parents at 0x21, 0x19 and 0x11 all gave children 0x15). Thread C comes from tokio's blocking pool and the submit thread from std, so both run at default. No QoS code was added; the code comment and docs say so instead of claiming the class is inherited.

6. std has no timed join, so Drop waits for the thread's `exited` flag on the Condvar for up to LATE_OUTPUT and then joins. This blocks thread C for up to 250 ms on drop, as the design asks, although the Rust guide prefers a Drop that never blocks.

7. macos_encoder_load is logged after the first call that comes a second or more after the previous line (there is no idle timer), and it carries a `seconds` field. It is a debug line on the feedback target, like macos_capture_timing. macos_capture_layout is a debug line on the session target.

8. No input made VideoToolbox refuse an encode. I tried a 64x64 picture, a BGRA picture, an 8192x8192 picture and AverageBitRate 0 and u32::MAX; it accepted all of them. The error-path test therefore uses a test-only tear_down hook, which invalidates the session on the submit thread so that the next real EncodeFrame fails. The thread's final invalidate is then a second one; a later commit corrected the safety note to say so.

9. MacVideo::submit needs a ScreenCaptureKit stream, which no test can build. So "submit returns false and keeps the keyframe" and "in_flight >= 2 returns true" are tested on Encoder::admit with a picture held in the mailbox: admit(1) gives Full, admit(VT_IN_FLIGHT) gives Busy, and a finished unit waiting to be drained is not counted.

10. Measurement: input-wait p99 was 40–53 µs in 58 of 60 after runs. Run 1 of H.265 at pace 60 gave 4.4 ms at 1920x1200 and 3.3 ms at 2560x1440 while the pacing loop was not in a call (load average 5.3); runs 2 and 3 of those cases gave 46 µs. This is recorded as measured, not smoothed over.

11. The before arm of the rate-model test gated on pending() < 3 (its ring size), the after arm on admit(2). With standard rate control at 4K and pace 30, H.265 submitted 115 and 116 pictures after against 120 and 119 before.

impl.measurements:
Environment: release builds on a 12-core Apple M6 with 24 GiB, macOS 27.0 (26A425), Rust 1.99.1. Synthetic IOSurface pictures and real hardware VideoToolbox, with low-latency rate control. Other agents' builds were running; load averages were 1.6–8.1 at the starts of the runs.

video_toolbox_submit_blocking: 3 runs per arm, alternating. Before is commit 3aeef96 (thread C calls VideoToolbox; gate pending() >= 4). Figures are medians.
- Submit call p50 before: 5.0–5.2 ms at 1920x1200, 7.2–7.5 ms at 2560x1440, 12.6–12.9 ms at 3328x2160, 14.3–15.0 ms at 3840x2160 (31–36 µs at 1920x1080). After: 3–5 µs at every size.
- Submit call p99: 6.0–21.4 ms before, 5–14 µs after (1920x1080: 62–78 µs before).
- Emulated input wait p99 before: 5.0–5.3 ms at 1920x1200, 7.3–7.7 ms at 2560x1440, 12.8–14.9 ms at 3328x2160, 14.9–17.4 ms at 3840x2160 (45–47 µs at 1920x1080). After: 44–49 µs as a median, 40–53 µs in 58 of 60 runs; the two exceptions are in deviation 10.
- Units per second within 1% of before everywhere. 4K at pace 120: H.264 66.0 to 65.4, H.265 68.4 to 68.2. 3328x2160 at pace 120: H.264 75.2 to 74.8, H.265 78.0 to 77.8. At those sizes nearly every due tick stayed armed (65–78 a second).
- Dwell p50 within 0.05 ms of before in every case. Dwell p95 within 0.2 ms except two cases at pace 120: 3328x2160 H.264 14.19 to 15.51 ms and 3328x2160 H.265 14.70 to 13.38 ms.

video_toolbox_in_flight: 1 run per arm. On the after build at pace 120, gate 4 against gate 2:
- 3024x1964 H.264: dwell p50 40.64 to 18.11 ms, 89.4 to 89.6 units/s.
- 3024x1964 H.265: 39.13 to 17.33 ms, 91.8 to 92.2 units/s.
- 3340x2160 H.264: 49.40 to 22.61 ms, 74.6 to 75.2 units/s.
- 3340x2160 H.265: 46.79 to 21.22 ms, 77.8 to 78.6 units/s.
- At pace 60, and at 1920x1080 at either pace, every case delivered its pace with no skipped ticks.
- Before the change, a gate of 4 also made the caller's call p99 1.5–2.0 ms.

video_toolbox_rate_model: H.264 and H.265 run once per arm, H.265 a second time per arm.
- Fitted model: always timestamp. The within-25% verdict matched in every case except H.265 1080p with low latency, which flipped between runs in both builds.
- Submits: unchanged except 4K low-latency at pace 60 (the test paints each picture on its own pacing thread: 197 against 192–200) and H.265 4K standard rate control at pace 30 (115 and 116 after against 120 and 119 before).
- Dwell p50 moved by under 1 ms in all but 4 steps.

findings.issue: `a_bitrate_set_during_an_encode_returns_at_once_and_reaches_the_session` never checks the brief's claim (set_bitrate returns in under 1 ms while the thread is inside a 4K call). It sorts the three timings and asserts only `took[0]`, the fastest. The call that matters is the first one, made while the encode is running. If it blocks, the encode is over by the next call, so the next two are fast and the test still passes.
findings.evidence: I ran an experiment and reverted it afterwards. Replacing set_bitrate's body with `while self.shared.state.lock().in_call { yield_now() }` before storing the rate makes set_bitrate wait out the call. The test still passed in 5 of 5 runs. A temporary print of the timings showed `took [42ns, 83ns, 36.87675ms]`, `[41ns, 42ns, 36.072875ms]` and `[0ns, 42ns, 36.032625ms]`: one call blocked for the whole debug-mode 4K encode, and the assertion did not notice.
findings.fix: Assert on every call, e.g. `assert!(took.iter().all(|t| *t < Duration::from_millis(1)))`, or at least on the first call, timed before sorting and only when `inside` held. Keep the sorted vector only for the message.

findings.issue: `a_busy_submit_thread_leaves_the_tick_armed_and_wakes_thread_c` does not show that the submit thread wakes thread C after a successful call. The 640x360 encode's output callback also calls `waker.wake()`, and that wake alone satisfies `waiter.wait(..3 s)`. The case the post-call wake exists for has no test: a submit refused while the thread applies a bitrate, a call that has no output callback. If the post-call wake (encoder.rs `if wake { ... waker.wake() }` in serve) regresses, thread C would sleep on idle_until's moving `now + LATE_OUTPUT` until some unrelated wake.
findings.evidence: I ran an experiment and reverted it afterwards: changing `if wake {` in serve() to `if false && wake {`. a_busy_submit_thread_leaves_the_tick_armed_and_wakes_thread_c still passed 3 of 3 runs. Across the whole platform::macos::tests suite only an_encode_refused_on_the_submit_thread_surfaces_from_drain failed, and that test covers the failure wake, not the c_waiting wake after a successful call.
findings.fix: Add a case with no output callback. Hold the thread, set a bitrate, release it, and refuse a submit while `in_call()` (a test hook can make the rate apply observable, as `hold` does for jobs). Then drain any earlier wake and assert that the waiter is woken and that `waiting()` cleared. Or use a test-only counter of the serve thread's c_waiting wakes and assert it rose.

findings.issue: A tick spent on the Mac's new in-flight gate (`Admit::Full => return Ok(true)`) is no longer counted in `skipped_ticks`, so the viewer's `skipped_per_s` loses it. The worker treats Ok(true) as a capture: `window.captured(now, None)`, `captures_per_s`, IDR marked answered. Before this PR the Mac's backpressure ran through the worker's own gate (`pending < ENCODER_DEPTH`, which tripped first), and those ticks were counted in `skipped_ticks`. The docs still say they are counted: rule 2 says a tick is skipped while 'the encoder holds four (two on a Mac host's VideoToolbox)'. The gate paragraph (remote-desktop.md:1408) says skipped ticks are 'counted in `skipped_ticks`'. The new Mac paragraph says 'a tick that finds two spends itself; see the gate above'. The table at about line 2259 still says '4 in the encoder'. The plan's research foresaw this ('skipped_ticks no longer shows a slow macOS encoder'), but nothing user-facing records it.
findings.evidence: after-in-flight-1.txt, 3024x1964 at pace 120 with depth 2: skipped_per_s=30.4 (H.264) and 27.6 (H.265), and 3340x2160 gives 45.0 and 41.6. In production those 30–45 ticks a second now go through `Admit::Full`, then Ok(true), then the worker's submitted branch (worker/capture.rs: `pacer.consume`, `window.captured`, `idr.answered`). The skip branch that does `slot.state.skipped_ticks += 1` is not reached. The viewer's quality panel and the docs' diagnosis rule ('a capture rate below the pace is the host's source or its gate (`skipped_per_s`, ...)') would therefore show 0 skipped on a MacBook's built-in display at 120 FPS, where the base showed about 30/s.
findings.fix: Choose one. (a) Document that a Mac host's VT gate ticks count as captures, not `skipped_ticks`, and appear in `macos_encoder_load`'s `gate_ticks` instead. Fix rule 2, the gate paragraph, the Mac paragraph's 'see the gate above' and the hand-off table. (b) Keep the stat: let the worker learn of source backpressure, e.g. a `VideoSource`/`Backend` `encoder_full()` (default false) checked next to `pending < ENCODER_DEPTH`, so these ticks take the worker's skip branch (same `pacer.consume(now, None)`) and are counted.

reviews.notes:
Base perf2/mac-wake-display (5491036), reviewed at 0280a23. I read every changed line in encoder.rs, video.rs and tests.rs, plus the doc, CHANGELOG and benchmark diffs. I also checked the worker's capture loop (worker/capture.rs capture_step/capture_at/capture_poll_after), native.rs capture_video, the Waker (sticky flag) and the receive() callback.

The concurrency logic is correct as far as I can tell:
- Every write to job, rate, in_call, c_waiting, stop and exited happens under the one state mutex, and the Condvar is only waited on with that mutex. Setters notify after unlocking and waiters check under the lock, so no notification is lost.
- c_waiting is set only while busy(), and every path that ends a busy spell clears it and wakes thread C: after a call, in the failure branch, and on failure.
- encode is only reachable after admit returns Free, so its "holds a picture already" error is unreachable.
- in_flight and pending count the mailbox's unit once, because its Pending is queued when the job is handed over.
- forget() with rposition is robust whether or not VT also calls back for a refused frame.
- The stop check comes before the test-only held branch.
- The final invalidate runs with no lock held, and Drop's wait_until releases the lock, so the callback cannot deadlock against Drop.
- On a Drop timeout the thread keeps Arc<Shared>, so the refcon stays valid until it returns.
- No ALPN, wire, FFI or helper-pipe change. Nothing outside platform/macos changed. The new #[link] to IOSurface and CVPixelBufferGetIOSurface/IOSurfaceGetAllocSize exist on macOS 10.15. platform/macos is not compiled for iOS.

Run here (Apple M6, macOS 27.0, Rust 1.99.1, debug builds):
- `cargo test -p pb-mapper-desktop --all-features --lib platform::macos::tests` passed 13 of 13, three times.
- `cargo clippy -p pb-mapper-desktop --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` is clean, and `cargo fmt --all -- --check` is clean.

Experiments, all reverted (the tree is clean at 0280a23):
- Disabling the post-call wake in serve (finding 2).
- Making set_bitrate wait out the call (finding 1).
- A probe of set_bitrate followed at once by admit: 0 of 200 Busy refusals, so a bitrate change does not normally inflate armed_refusals.
- Forcing software H.264 to emulate CI made even the pre-existing keyframe test fail with "stalled". That emulation does not represent the CI runner and I drew no conclusion from it.

Not verified, and possible flake risks on CI's macOS VM (rust-macos-desktop): the new 4K H.264 bitrate test (Encoder::new(...).expect at 3840x2160, then reading back AverageBitRate), and the drop test's `took < LATE_OUTPUT + 50 ms` with a 1920x1088 synchronous encode on a slower encoder. Neither can be checked here.

Benchmark figures in the README, CHANGELOG and VT_IN_FLIGHT comment match the raw files. The before figures for input wait at 1920x1200 are medians of three, which hides a 12.4 ms run; the README says so, but the CHANGELOG does not say "median".

Build output deleted (target/, ui/build).

findings.issue: The busy-thread wake is the core of the Busy design, and no test fails without it. When a submit finds the submit thread busy, thread C keeps its tick armed and its source names a time 250 ms away, so only the submit thread's wake after the call brings the next submit (encoder.rs:795). The test's `waiter.wait(3 s)` is also satisfied by VideoToolbox's output-callback wake (receive -> waker.wake). At a size that is a multiple of 16, that callback fires inside the call, before c_waiting is cleared, and thread C then sees waiting() still true and goes back to sleep. A regression that dropped the wake would therefore slow a 1440p/4K Mac host to thread C's other wakes, and nothing in CI would catch it (only the ignored measurements would).
findings.evidence: Mutation run here: at encoder.rs:795, `let mut wake = std::mem::take(&mut state.c_waiting);` was replaced with `let _ = std::mem::take(&mut state.c_waiting); let mut wake = false;`. `cargo test -p pb-mapper-desktop --all-features --lib platform::macos::tests` still passed 13/13, three runs out of three. The file was restored afterwards.
findings.fix: Make the submit thread's own wake observable apart from the output wake. Option 1: add a #[cfg(test)] counter that the submit thread increments where it wakes thread C for c_waiting (both sites), and assert it went from 0 to 1 over the busy spell. Option 2: add a #[cfg(test)] hook that parks the thread after its VT call returns but before it clears in_call, at a multiple-of-16 size (for example 640x368) so the output callback has already woken. Then drain that wake, assert waiting() and that no further wake arrives while parked, release, and assert a wake arrives with waiting() false.

findings.issue: a_bitrate_set_during_an_encode_returns_at_once_and_reaches_the_session cannot fail without the change. It checks only the fastest of three calls (`took.sort_unstable(); took[0] < 1 ms`), and a synchronous AverageBitRate/DataRateLimits set during a 4K encode is itself well under 1 ms. So it would not catch a regression that moves the property set back onto the caller (thread C). The latest-wins read-back passes either way too.
findings.evidence: Mutation run here: in cfg(test), set_bitrate was made to call `apply(&self.session, bitrate)` directly on the calling thread while the submit thread was inside a 3840x2160 encode. The printed timings were took=[119 µs, 83 µs, 63 µs], [108, 91, 74] and [134, 71, 88] µs with inside=true and still=true. The test passed 3/3. The file was restored afterwards.
findings.fix: Assert that set_bitrate defers the call instead of timing it. Call encoder.hold(true), then set_bitrate, then assert average_bitrate() still reads the old 10 Mbps (the calling thread touched nothing). Call hold(false), wait_for(idle), and assert 16 Mbps. Also check every timing (the max, or the first call before sorting), not the minimum.

findings.issue: A saturated Mac encoder no longer shows up in skipped_ticks, the 'skipped /s' figure the viewer's quality panel displays. Before, VideoToolbox holding four units tripped the worker's ENCODER_DEPTH gate, which increments skipped_ticks. Now MacVideo spends the tick itself at two units (`Admit::Full => return Ok(true)`). The worker treats that as a submit: it consumes the pacer, counts window.captured(now, None) and marks the IDR answered, but never increments skipped_ticks. At an asynchronous size and pace 120, where about 30-45 ticks/s are spent this way, the panel reads 0 /s where it read about 30 /s for the same saturation. Rule 2 in docs/remote-desktop.md:1329 ('A tick is skipped only while ... the encoder holds four (two on a Mac host's VideoToolbox)'), read with the 'counted in skipped_ticks' sentence at about line 1409, says the opposite. The CHANGELOG does not mention it.
findings.evidence: worker/capture.rs: `pending < ENCODER_DEPTH` gates (line ~311); skipped_ticks += 1 only in the `if tick_due` branch after the gate fails (lines ~368-376); a submitted=true result goes to pacer.consume/window.captured. ui/lib/src/pages/remote/viewer/quality_panel.dart:283-308 shows skipped_per_s. The test loop's video_toolbox_in_flight shows 30.4-45.0 skipped/s at gate 2 (after-in-flight-1.txt); in production those ticks are now uncounted.
findings.fix: Option 1: count the spend. Let the source report a tick spent on backpressure, for example a VideoSource flag that native.rs surfaces through the Backend next to submitted_video(), which the worker adds to skipped_ticks. The worker's generic gate stays unchanged. Option 2: if leaving it uncounted is intended, say so in rule 2 and in the skipped_ticks paragraph of docs/remote-desktop.md (a Mac host's two-in-flight spends are not in skipped_ticks and appear only as macos_encoder_load.gate_ticks), and in the CHANGELOG bullet.

reviews.notes:
The branch builds the whole brief and should have the intended effect. Thread C now does no VideoToolbox call after open: EncodeFrame with ForceKeyFrame, AverageBitRate/DataRateLimits and the final invalidate all run on the "pb-mapper-vt-submit" thread inside autoreleasepool, with no lock held across a production call. The probe gets no thread. The one-slot mailbox is a CFRetain with no allocation. Pending is still pushed at hand-off, so dwell, late() and the OUTPUT_WAIT stall check are unchanged. Failures reach drain through codec_error, so H.265 still ends with EncoderFailed. MacVideo::submit gates on admit(VT_IN_FLIGHT=2): Full spends the tick; Busy keeps both the tick and self.keyframe. idle_until names now+LATE_OUTPUT while waiting(). Drop waits up to LATE_OUTPUT and then detaches. The traces macos_encoder_load and macos_capture_layout are in. The worker gate, QUEUE_DEPTH and Windows' MAX_IN_FLIGHT are untouched; nothing outside platform/macos changed besides docs.

Deviations, checked against the code:
- 1 (in_flight = pending.len()) is correct: the brief's own formula would count the mailbox unit twice.
- 2 (waiting() instead of busy() in idle_until) gives at most one empty poll per busy spell and no spin. A wake that arrives in between is not lost, because both sides take the same lock.
- 5 (QoS): I reproduced it with a C probe here. A pthread's child reads 0x15 (default) whether its creator ran at 0x21, 0x19, 0x11 or 0x09. So the comment and docs saying the submit thread runs at default QoS, as thread C does, are accurate.

Edge case, not reported: if VideoToolbox hung inside a bitrate-only set with nothing pending, thread C would keep pushing its deadline 250 ms out and never retry, and no stall check would fire. Before, such a hang froze thread C outright.

impl.device_only:
Live effects need a Mac host with Screen Recording granted:
- A Mac host playing video at Balanced over a shaped 4 Mbit/s path: the viewer's received_fps against the host's macos_encoder_dropped.
- A Mac host over a shaped 2 Mbit/s path: take control and type at once, then read the echo delay.
- A 4K or MacBook Pro 14 host with a 120 Hz viewer on Smooth: capture fps, encoder_dwell_ms, and bitrate against target, confirming H.265 stays on low latency.
- Whether the measured behaviour holds on other Apple chips (only the M6 was measured), and on Intel Macs, where MaxAllowedFrameQP may be refused (tolerated).
- CI: the rust-macos-desktop job, and nat-traversal.yml on Linux.

findings.issue: A resubmit can be left due after a newer picture is handed over, which leads to one redundant resubmit. `MacVideo::submit` takes the flag at its start (`take_resubmit`, video.rs:306), but the unit is pushed only later, in `encode`. On an asynchronous session (any size that is not a multiple of 16, such as 1920x1080 or 3024x1964), VideoToolbox's output thread can report a drop in that gap. It sees `pending` empty, so `newest` is true and `due` is set. Thread C then hands over Fresh B, and `submitted(Unit::Fresh)` resets `made` but leaves `due` set. At the next tick with no new picture, B is sent again as `Unit::Resubmit` (not a duplicate) while B itself is still in flight or already kept. That costs an extra encode and bits, counts toward `unique`/`received_fps` and extends `hot_until`.
findings.evidence: resubmit.rs:58-64: `Unit::Fresh => self.made = 0` and `due` is untouched. receive() (encoder.rs:1354) decides `newest` under the state lock, and encode() (encoder.rs:777) pushes the Pending and calls `submitted(unit)` under that same lock, but only after take_resubmit has already cleared `due` earlier in the same submit. The interleaving 'take_resubmit, then the drop callback, then encode(B)' leaves `due == true` with B in flight. The pure state shows it: dropped(Fresh, true), then submitted(Fresh), then take() returns true.
findings.fix: Have `Resubmit::submitted` clear `due` when a picture is handed over: `Unit::Fresh => { self.made = 0; self.due = false }` and `Unit::Resubmit => { self.made = self.made.saturating_add(1); self.due = false }`. This runs under the same lock as the Pending push, so a drop that arrives after the newer unit was handed over can no longer leave a stale flag. Add a case to `a_duplicate_or_a_superseded_drop_is_not_resubmitted`: dropped(Fresh, true), then submitted(Fresh), then assert !take().

findings.issue: `Unit::of(false, false)` always gives `Repeat`, flagged duplicate, whether or not the encoder ever kept the last picture. Once the two resubmits are spent, a liveness or keyframe repeat carries a picture the viewer never had, yet it goes out as `duplicate = true`. If that repeat is dropped, it is not resubmitted, because `dropped()` returns early for a duplicate. This contradicts the rule the PR documents: `Unit::duplicate` says 'Whether the viewer was sent this picture already', and remote-desktop.md says 'A dropped duplicate is never sent again: the viewer has it'. The viewer's `received_fps` and the host's `unique`/`hot_until` miss that picture.
findings.evidence: docs/benchmarks/2026-11-24-macos-rate-model/resubmit.txt, after arm at 1 Mbit/s: trials k=4 (540 ms) and k=9 (290.7 ms) are `carried_by=repeat` for both codecs. The last new picture reached the viewer only in a unit that `Unit::Repeat.duplicate()` flags as a duplicate (resubmit.rs:37-39). `Resubmit::dropped` returns false for `unit.duplicate()` (resubmit.rs:70).
findings.fix: Track in `Resubmit` whether the newest picture handed over has been kept: set `delivered = false` on submitted(Fresh) and `delivered = true` on kept(any). Have `take`/`Unit::of` treat a repeat of an undelivered picture as non-duplicate, for example by returning the flag from `take_resubmit` or adding `Encoder::last_delivered()`. Then the flag is correct, and a dropped repeat of an undelivered picture goes through the same resubmit bound. If the brief's 'never for a duplicate' rule is kept as written, at least correct the docs' claim that the viewer has every dropped duplicate.

findings.issue: The QP-bound test fails on an encoder that rejects the value but still reports the property, a refusal that production explicitly tolerates. `build` treats a failed `set(MaxAllowedFrameQP, 51)` as 'keeps its own bound' (`max_qp = ... is_ok()`). The test skips only when `max_qp()` returns None and otherwise asserts 51. The implementer's own note says an unbound low-latency session on the M6 reads back -1, so the key can be read when it is not set. An encoder that refuses 51 but reports its own value (the Intel or software-encoder case the docs mention) would fail `assert_eq!(qp, 51)` on CI's macos-latest runner, which has not run this test yet.
findings.evidence: encoder.rs build(): `max_qp = low_latency && bound_qp && cf::symbol(MAX_QP).is_some_and(|key| set(&session, key, &cf::number(MAX_QP_VALUE)).is_ok());`, where a refusal is tolerated. tests.rs:455-463: `let Some(qp) = bound.max_qp() else { report; return }; assert_eq!(qp, 51);`. The test's doc comment says a Mac that refuses is to be reported, not failed.
findings.fix: Keep the `max_qp` bool that build already computes for the log in the Encoder under #[cfg(test)], or expose it through a test accessor. In the test, report and return when the session did not take the bound, and assert `max_qp() == Some(51)` only when it did.

**What holds:**

- The resubmit flag moves into `MacVideo` before admit, so a Full or Busy admit keeps it, and `idle_until` returns None while it is due.

- The `newest` test counts the mailbox job through `pending`.
- A synchronous session (size a multiple of 16) reports every drop as newest, because no later unit can be handed over during the call. Resubmits there are absorbed by the next fresh picture when one is ready; otherwise they re-send the dropped picture within the bound of two. That matches the brief.

The scroll PSNR gap (37 against 52 dB while standard spends more bits) looks suspicious as a measurement, but rejecting step 4 does not depend on it.

findings.issue: No test that runs by default covers how the resubmit is wired into production. The brief's "none with a later unit in flight" check, the mailbox case and the wake are all decided in receive(): `newest = state.pending.is_empty()` after the pop, and `keyframe || resubmit` as the return. The codec/resubmit.rs tests only pass `newest` in as a bool. Turning the whole feature off fails no test.
findings.evidence: Mutation run here: in receive(), `let resubmit = state.resubmit.dropped(pending.unit, newest);` became `false`; in MacVideo::submit (video.rs:306), `self.resubmit |= self.encoder.take_resubmit();` became a discard. Then `cargo test -p pb-mapper-desktop --all-features --lib` gave "233 passed; 0 failed; 30 ignored". Only the ignored release measurement video_toolbox_resubmit, through its emulation of MacVideo, would notice. By contrast, the QP-bound test does catch its mutation: with the bound forced off, it fails with left -1, right 51.

findings.issue: A resubmit can outlive the newer picture that should cancel it. MacVideo::submit calls take_resubmit() before admit()/stream.take() and only later calls encode(). If VideoToolbox drops the only unit in flight in that window, the drop counts as newest and sets `due`. The encode(Fresh) that follows resets `made` but leaves `due` set. The next tick then sends the newer picture again as a non-duplicate Resubmit, even if it is still in flight or already kept. That costs one wasted unit, adds one to unique/received_fps and uses one of that picture's two resubmits.
findings.evidence: video.rs:306: `self.resubmit |= self.encoder.take_resubmit();` comes before `admit` and `stream.take`, and encode() is called at video.rs:348-349. resubmit.rs:58-63: `submitted(Unit::Fresh)` only sets `self.made = 0` and never clears `self.due`. encoder.rs:1354 marks a drop newest whenever `pending` is empty, which it is while the new picture's Pending has not been pushed yet. With VT_IN_FLIGHT = 2, one unit is normally in flight when thread C submits the next, so the window opens on every submit.
findings.fix: In `Resubmit::submitted`, clear `due` for `Unit::Fresh` (a newer picture replaces the dropped one) and for `Unit::Resubmit`, for example `Unit::Fresh => { self.made = 0; self.due = false; }`. Add a pure test: dropped(Fresh, true), then submitted(Fresh), then take() returns false.

findings.issue: No commit can reproduce the recorded 120 FPS run. It came from a build that carried the rejected step-4 code (the knee rule and STD_RATE_FACTOR), and that code is in no commit. Its `past_knee` column, and the README's verdict that "the rule fired at 2560x1664", come from that code. The README also claims the std_* arms equal today's capped=false knob, and nobody can check that.
findings.evidence: `git log -S past_knee perf2/mac-vt-submit-thread..HEAD` lists only 04314b8, the docs commit that adds 120.txt. `git log -S STD_RATE_FACTOR` lists nothing. The committed vt_measure.rs case_120 prints no past_knee field, but each of 120.txt's 480 result lines carries one. README.md:97-101 discloses that the run's build carried the switch.

findings.issue:
Several statements in the docs and comments go beyond the raw data:
1. remote-desktop.md:1722 and the README (line 150) say the 1.5 s after an IDR dropped about the same with and without the bound. That holds for busy and text only: for noise, the bound cut post-IDR drops by about a third.
2. remote-desktop.md:1779 says the measurements paint pictures "into a pool as ScreenCaptureKit fills its own". The follow-pace sweeps in tests.rs, which produce the rate-model table, paint a ring of 3 surfaces.
3. The documented filter at remote-desktop.md:2058, `--test-threads=1 video_toolbox_rate_model`, now also selects the two follow tests, each about 5.5 min.

findings.fix:
1. Scope the post-IDR sentence to busy and text, and add that for noise the bound also cut post-IDR drops from about two thirds to half.
2. Say the vt_measure tests use the pool and the follow sweeps use 3 surfaces painted per picture.
3. Name the filters `video_toolbox_rate_model_h26` and `video_toolbox_rate_model_follow`.
4. Cite 169 from drops.txt in the encoder.rs comment, or name the run the 168 comes from.

findings.issue:
The CHANGELOG bullet says more than the measurements show:
1. "at 2 and 4 Mbit/s nothing changed" holds only for the count of slow trials. At 4 Mbit/s, one trial per codec now needed a resubmit and took about 22 ms, where every trial before came within 7 ms. At 2 Mbit/s, the slow trial grew from 257 ms to 291 ms. The README records both.
2. "scrolling text, and text with images under grain, lost none before or after" holds only in steady state. Right after an IDR, those contents lost pictures in both arms.
findings.fix: Write "at 2 and 4 Mbit/s as many trials took that long as before", and "lost none in steady state, before or after".

findings.issue: `Shared.capped` and `Options.capped` exist only for a test arm, yet they are production fields. They are always true outside tests, and `apply()` branches on them on the submit thread for every bitrate change. They are left over from the rejected step 4 (standard rate control without DataRateLimits). `quality` and `max_qp`, the other test knobs, are already cfg(test).
findings.evidence: `Options::new` sets `capped: true` unconditionally. Only `vt_measure.rs` (the `std_*` arms) and `Options` literals in tests set it to false. `serve` calls `apply(&session, bitrate, shared.capped)`.

reviews.notes:
Overall: steps 1 and 2 are built as the brief designs them, and the fixes needed are small. Steps 3, 4 and 5 were measured and not adopted, each on recorded data that fails the brief's own gates, so leaving them out is justified.

Done as designed:
- Step 1: the low-latency session sets kVTCompressionPropertyKey_MaxAllowedFrameQP to 51 (looked up with cf::symbol), a refusal is tolerated, and standard rate control never sets it. `max_qp` is logged, `dropped` is counted, and `macos_encoder_dropped` is traced at most once a second from drain. Deviation 5 (setting it in build rather than on the submit thread) is sound, because build configures the session before that thread exists.
- Step 2: the pure helper lives in codec/resubmit.rs and is tested on every platform. The flag is never marked duplicate, is bounded at two, and a newer picture wins. idle_until returns None while a resubmit is pending or wanted, and pipeline.rs's liveness text is updated.

Not adopted, and why that holds:
- Step 3 (Timestamp start): H.265 low latency fails the gate in this run and in the earlier ring runs. Spend fell to 0.02–0.04 of target at the lowest paces, and an IDR at 10 FPS was followed by 16–18 drops of 20.

name: mac-capture-cadence
title: Mac host: ScreenCaptureKit cadence from the display's refresh and the live pace, a 2 fps pause, a faster start, a filled frame, and no capture rebuild on an fps-only limits change

commits: 9cce25d Pace a Mac host's ScreenCaptureKit stream from the display's refresh
