impl.summary:
All paths are under /Users/lb7666/rust_pro/pb-mapper/.claude/worktrees/wf_352d1379-280-4. The branch perf2/viewer-feedback is based on perf2/wave1 (bdbcd76) and its head is d299970. The worktree is detached and clean, and target and ui/build are deleted.

Testkit and measurement cases
- crates/pb-mapper-testkit/src/shaped.rs and lib.rs: new `shaped_link_each_way(relay, up, down)`. `shaped_link` now wraps it.
- crates/pb-mapper-desktop/src/slow_link.rs:
  - `Rig::each_way` builds a rig whose two directions are shaped apart.
  - `Interval` now also records bpf, the window, the adaptation, rtt, delay, the ack queue and the forward and reverse queues. `Interval::print` writes them, and the bandwidth case now prints its intervals.
  - Two new ignored cases: `reverse_path_queue_is_not_congestion` and `reverse_queue_with_forward_limit_still_cuts`.

Protocol (protocol.rs)
- Two capabilities, `arrival_time` and `keyframe_seq`. `MAX_CAPABILITIES` is now pub(crate).
- New optional fields, omitted when unset: `Received.at_us`, `ProbeEcho.at_us`, `Keyframe.after_seq`, and `StatsRecord.forward_queue_ms` / `reverse_queue_ms`.
- Round-trip and omission tests, and an updated stats golden.

New oneway.rs
- `WindowMin`: a monotone deque over the 60 s window, one entry per 250 ms bucket, 256 entries reserved once.
- `OneWay` holds the forward minimum (shared by receipts and probes), the reverse minimum (receipts only) and a 3-slot ring of recent reverse queues.
- A sample that goes backwards for its kind, or lies more than IO_TIMEOUT above the minimum, is ignored. `reset()` clears it.
- Tests: minimum tracking, the bound, clock offsets of either sign, refused stamps, reset, and the window term.

credit.rs
- `CreditLedger::new(now, arrival_time)`. `on_receipt(seq, now, at_us)` fills `Receipt.arrival` (the stamp, forward_queue, reverse_queue).
- With arrival times, the ack samples are forward queues and the ack queue is their median minus the RTT floor's gap. The window's t adds min(least of the newest three reverse queues, 1 s).
- Keyframe skipping: `last_keyframe`, `skip_to_keyframe(after_seq)` (returns `KeyframeAhead` past the last admitted seq), and `skipping()`. The skip is cleared when an IDR is booked, or after 2 s.
- Also new: `probe_queue`, `one_way_queues`, `reset_one_way`, `set_floor_gap`.

qos.rs
- `use_one_way()`. `on_probe_echo(nonce, now, forward, ack_queue)`: in one-way mode, the history, delay and raw values are forward queues minus the floor gap. RTT still feeds the base RTT, the short path and the fast start.
- RTT samples are now stored unfloored; `base_rtt` applies the 10 ms floor. New `floor_gap()` and `probe_sent_at()`.
- qos/receipt_rate.rs: in one-way mode the shadow estimator uses the viewer-clock arrival and the forward queue, and leaves out receipts whose stamp was refused.

Host side
- session.rs:
  - Negotiates both capabilities and passes at_us only when both ends listed arrival_time.
  - ProbeEcho computes the probe's forward queue and sets the floor gap.
  - Keyframe{after_seq} sets the skip for non-JPEG sessions, wakes B-send, and treats a seq ahead of the last admitted one as `Violation::Keyframe`.
  - Path and Resume reset the one-way state.
- session/sender.rs: B-send drops non-keyframe heads while skipping, counted in dropped_frames. Stats and the feedback trace carry forward_queue_ms and reverse_queue_ms.
- host/acceptor.rs: `SESSION_CAPABILITIES` is listed back to a viewer that asked, with a test that the longest list each end sends stays within the bound.

Viewer
- config.rs lists both capabilities. mod.rs builds `Outbound::new(arrival_epoch, keyframe_seq)` from Accepted.
- session.rs: the Reader stamps a probe when its header has been read, and a receipt when the unit's payload has been read.
- outbound.rs:

  - `keyframe(reason, discarding)` adds after_seq, keeping a pending seq when a request is merged.
  - at_us is written only to a host that listed the capability.
- sink.rs: `SinkState::discarding()` is false for User, follows wait_key for Backlog, and is true for Gap, DecoderError and Stall. It is used for direct requests and timer retries.
- stats.rs and status.rs: `ViewerStats.forward_queue_ms` and `reverse_queue_ms`.
- Tests:
  - viewer/tests.rs: an old host never gets at_us or after_seq; a capable one gets both; the receipt's stamp follows the whole unit.
  - session/tests.rs: skip until the IDR; protocol error past the last seq; an old viewer gets no Stats fields.

App
- desktop_models.dart: `forwardQueueMs` and `reverseQueueMs`.
- quality_panel.dart: a 'one-way-queue' row (Queue to this device, with the way back as detail), en and zh strings.
- viewer_chrome_test.dart: checks the row and that it is absent without the fields.

impl.deviations:
1. The receipt is stamped when the unit has been read whole, not at its header, and there is no split TLS write. I first built it as designed (commit 0b63ed4). Measured:
   - host_send_bench rose from 18.86 to 20.12 allocations per unit (median): about one more encrypted record per unit.
   - The 1 Mbit/s bandwidth case recovered in 5 s in 4 of 16 runs, against 0 of 16 before.
   - Header stamps also put each unit's transfer into the reverse queue, which the window adds to its time, and took it out of the forward queue the 100 ms ack-queue limit was tuned on.
   - With whole-unit stamps the reverse queue is just the viewer's writer and uplink, the forward queue keeps the transfer as round trips always did, allocations are back to 18.87 per unit, and no split is needed.
2. Added a floor gap, which the design did not mention. Round trips are floored at 10 ms (DELAY_FLOOR), which hides the first (10 ms minus the least round trip) of any queue on such a path. On loopback the one-way delay read about 8 ms higher and crossed the 200 ms band edge where the round trip did not.
   - Traced: the round trip's first cut read 197 to 212 ms; one-way without the gap read 205 to 218 ms.
   - Whole-unit stamps without the gap still recovered in 5 s in 3 of 16 runs.
   - Fix: RTT samples are stored unfloored and `Qos::floor_gap()` is subtracted from the one-way probe delay and from the one-way ack queue (via `CreditLedger::set_floor_gap`). This only matters on paths under 10 ms.
3. `Receipt` carries one `Option<Arrival>` holding the stamp, forward_queue and reverse_queue, instead of two separate Option fields.
4. Only receipts feed the reverse minimum; probe echoes feed only the forward one.
5. Stats meanings: forward_queue_ms is the one-way ack queue, and reverse_queue_ms is the median of the newest three reverse queues. The window uses the least of those three, capped at 1 s.
6. after_seq is set for Gap, DecoderError and Stall (the native decoders drop predicted frames after these), for Backlog only while the sink is in wait_key (an overflow), and never for User. The same rule covers timer retries.
7. The host lists both capabilities only back to a viewer that listed them, as peer_cursors does. A stamp or after_seq from a viewer that did not list the capability is ignored.
8. The reverse case's received-fps bound starts 3 s into the queue, not 2. The viewer's once-a-second figure 2 s in can still cover the first second, a one-round-trip credit stall measured at 48.7 to 50.7 FPS in that sample. The host's pace, clamp and bitrate checks cover every interval under the queue.
9. The test fake (ui/test/fake_desktop_api.dart) and the FFI needed no change: no new op, and the status JSON carries the new fields.
10. Measured results below the brief's expectations:
    - requested_idr frames_first fell from 33-39 to 23-24, not to near 0. The remaining frames were already in flight on the 1 Mbit/s link when the request reached the host.
    - With the committed logic, 1 of 32 bandwidth-limit runs recovered in 5 s (0 of 16 in the final set, 1 of 16 in the same logic's traced runs). The baseline had 0 of 16, plus 0 of 10 for this build with the viewer listing neither capability.
    - One header-variant run failed per_second_encoder_latches_under_an_fps_cap at a mean pace of 12.86. The viewer's own fps cap sat at 12 while the host's controller stayed at 60. No final run failed it.

reviews.notes:
Reviewed every changed line of perf2/wave1..perf2/viewer-feedback (d299970), plus the code around it: protocol.rs, oneway.rs, credit.rs, qos.rs, qos/receipt_rate.rs, session.rs, session/sender.rs, host/acceptor.rs, the viewer's outbound/session/sink/stats/status/mod/config, testkit shaped.rs, slow_link.rs, the Dart model, the quality panel and its test, the l10n files, docs and CHANGELOG. I also checked how the native runners behave after a keyframe request (ui/windows/runner/desktop_video.cpp, ui/linux/runner/desktop_video_gst.cpp, ui/darwin/DesktopVideo.swift) and how the IDR policy and capture worker work (idr.rs, worker/capture.rs).

Run here in my worktree: `cargo fmt --all -- --check` was clean. `cargo clippy -p pb-mapper-desktop -p pb-mapper-testkit -p pb-mapper-ffi --all-targets --all-features -D warnings` was clean. `cargo test -p pb-mapper-desktop --all-features` passed: lib 225 passed with 23 ignored, tests/session.rs 6 passed. `cargo test -p pb-mapper-ffi` passed 76. I did not rerun the release slow_link suite or host_send_bench, Flutter, the workspace-wide clippy or cargo doc. I deleted target and ui/build afterwards, and changed or committed nothing.

What checks out:
- **Capability gating.** Each end lists the new capabilities only when the other did, both ways. Session flags use `both()`. A stamp or after_seq from a viewer that did not negotiate it is filtered out. The Stats fields go out only when the ledger has one_way state. ALPN, deny_unknown_fields and HELPER_PROTOCOL are untouched, and the longest-list test is right (9 entries from the viewer, 8 from the host).
- **Keyframe skip.** after_seq is taken from read_seq at the moment of the request. Booking comes before writing, so a legitimate viewer can never trip `KeyframeAhead`. The skip runs per session in B-send, ahead of booking, so seqs stay contiguous. A keyframe head is never skipped, and booking an IDR clears the skip. The B-send wake is correct.
- **Locks and allocation.** There are no nested qos and credit locks. WindowMin is bounded (241 entries at most, 256 reserved) and amortised O(1).
- **Arithmetic and floor gap.** The i64 and u64 arithmetic saturates. The floor-gap arithmetic gives exactly the RTT mode's delay and ack-queue values on paths under 10 ms.
- **RTT samples.** Storing them unfloored leaves base_rtt as it was.
- **Native runners.** The Windows, Linux and macOS runners do wait for a key after a Gap and after a failure.
- **Windows.** No Windows-only code changed, and no cfg(windows) code builds the changed types.

Findings are all minor. The most substantive is the coupled validity check, which leaves one-way sessions without forward feedback once the uplink queue passes 3 s. Next is the 2 s skip expiry, which resumes predicted frames after a hole in the reference chain. The rest are documentation accuracy and a measurement bound the brief set.

Needs a device or CI, not checked here: a real saturating uplink over QUIC and relay TCP; the CI Windows, Android and Linux builds; Flutter on SDK 3.44.9.

findings.issue: One validity check covers both directions, and the RTT timeout returns before the one-way branch. The result: once the queue on the viewer's uplink is more than IO_TIMEOUT (3 s) above its least, a one-way session gets no forward congestion signal at all. The RTT mode still had one in that case. This is a busy cellular uplink, the very case the feature targets.
findings.evidence: `OneWay::receipt` returns None when either direction is out of range: `if !within(&self.forward, forward) || !within(&self.reverse, reverse) { return None; }` (oneway.rs:146). The receipt's forward queue, a real queue toward the viewer, is lost along with the reverse one. `CreditLedger::on_receipt` then pushes no ack sample (`(Some(_), Some(receipt)) => receipt.arrival.map(..)`, so `ack_samples` keeps its last 3 accepted samples indefinitely), and the receipt-rate estimator skips it. For probes, `Qos::on_probe_echo` returns at `if elapsed > IO_TIMEOUT { return; }` (qos.rs:631), before the `(true, Some(forward))` branch. The round trip carries the uplink queue, so every probe is dropped too. The RTT mode in the same situation still pushes the receipts' delays, which have no bound, so `ack_queue > ACK_QUEUE_LIMIT` clamps the byte window to the delivery rate. The one-way mode keeps the unclamped normal window, which the reverse term widens by up to 1 s. Bits per frame and fps get no sample. A downlink limit that arrives together with a 3.5 s uplink queue (an LTE upload with bufferbloat) therefore queues up to a byte window of data toward the viewer and nothing cuts.
findings.fix: Validate and record the two directions apart. Push the forward sample (and the ack sample) whenever the forward delay is within IO_TIMEOUT of its least, and the reverse sample (and the reverse ring) whenever the reverse delay is. In `on_probe_echo`, when `one_way` is on and a forward sample is present, skip only the RTT push for an elapsed time over IO_TIMEOUT, not the forward delay sample. Add a credit or qos test with a 3.5 s reverse queue and a 150 ms forward queue that still clamps and cuts.

findings.issue: When the 2 s skip expires without an IDR booked, B-send resumes sending predicted frames that refer to frames it dropped. That never helps the viewer decode, and it corrupts the picture on a decoder that was not actually waiting for a key. The Rust sink's own Stall request is such a case on the Windows and macOS runners, and the docs claim the opposite.
findings.evidence: `skipping()` clears `skip_until` once `now >= until` (credit.rs:307-309), after which sender.rs books non-key heads again. `SinkState::discarding` returns true for `KeyframeReason::Stall`. The sink's watchdog (`SinkState::stalled`, sink.rs:296) fires while the consumer still takes frames. On that request the Windows runner (desktop_video.cpp:1017-1026, 658) and the macOS runner (DesktopVideo.swift:918, 948, 1028) set awaiting_key only on a generation change, a discontinuity, a lost decoder or a failure, so they keep decoding predicted frames. docs/remote-desktop.md:1968 says 'every decoder's after a gap, a failure or a stall, which the native decoders drop predicted frames after until their next keyframe', which does not hold for the sink-originated Stall. While an IDR follows the skip the stream stays decodable. Once the skip expires first, every later P-frame references a dropped one.
findings.fix: Make a skip end only at an IDR. On expiry, keep dropping and ask C again with `shared.idr.lock().request(IdrReason::HostResync)`, as the OUTGOING_MAX_AGE path does, instead of resuming predicted frames. Alternatively, send after_seq for Stall only when the sink itself is in wait_key. Correct the docs sentence either way.

findings.issue: The brief set an acceptance bound for the bandwidth-limit case: 5 s recoveries must stay at 0 of 16 runs. The committed logic exceeded it in one of its two recorded sets.
findings.evidence: The table row reads 'Variant: floor gap on probes and ack queue | 11 | 4 | 1'. The text at lines 90-92 says 'over the two sets this logic recovered slowly in 1 of 32 runs, against 0 of 16 before'. The brief's MEASUREMENT says '5 s recoveries must stay 0 of 16 runs'.

findings.evidence: Deviation 1 in the implementer's report and the benchmark README (lines 147-149) say that stamping the whole unit 'needs no split'. wire.rs is unchanged in the diff.

findings.issue: The CHANGELOG says the viewer kept receiving 59.5 to 60.9 FPS under the uplink queue. The measured first second of the queue read 48.7 to 50.7 FPS, and the quoted range only holds from 3 s into the queue.
findings.evidence: The benchmark README says 'the sample that covers it read 49.5, 48.7 and 50.7 FPS'. Received FPS is 'sampled once a second from 3 s into the queue'. In slow_link.rs, `received` is filtered to `queued + 3 s .. lifted`.

findings.issue: No test that CI runs covers how the session connects arrival times to the QoS controller and the credit ledger. That wiring is `qos.use_one_way()` in `Session::new_in_room`, `credit.set_floor_gap(..)` and the probe's forward queue in the ProbeEcho handler, and `reset_one_way()` on Path and Resume. Only the ignored slow-link case `reverse_path_queue_is_not_congestion` catches a break, and CI never runs ignored cases. So a later change could silently send viewers back to round-trip QoS, the 4 FPS collapse under a busy uplink, while every gate stays green. The unit tests call `Qos::use_one_way`, `CreditLedger::set_floor_gap` and `OneWay::reset` directly, and `session/tests.rs` checks only that `forward_queue_ms` reaches Stats, which comes from the ledger.
findings.evidence: Mutation run here: I changed `if arrival_time { qos.use_one_way(); }` to `if arrival_time && false { .. }` in session.rs. Then `cargo test -p pb-mapper-desktop --lib --all-features` gave 225 passed, 0 failed, 23 ignored. Reading the code, removing either `self.credit.lock().reset_one_way()` call (session.rs:443, 460) or the `set_floor_gap` call is also caught only by ignored cases.
findings.fix: Add a session test in `session/tests.rs`, built like `a_keyframe_request_after_a_seq_skips_predicted_units_until_the_idr` with both capabilities listed. The test viewer answers probes and receipts with `at_us` taken at read time, then holds its echoes and receipts back about 300 ms while keeping `at_us` at read time. The committed change has no split video header: deviation 1 removed it in cb280a3, and receipts are stamped once the unit is read whole. Brief coverage, step by step against the diff:
- A1: both capabilities are listed by the viewer. The host lists them back to a viewer that listed them (`SESSION_CAPABILITIES` in `negotiated_capabilities`, used on both the first-viewer and room paths).
- A2: the Reader stamps probes at header time and receipts at payload time. The Outbound slots keep (value, Instant) and write `at_us` only when the host listed the capability.
- A3 (split TLS write): deliberately not built. The measured reasons hold up:

  - 5 s recoveries rose to 4 of 16 runs;
  - header stamps moved the unit's transfer out of the forward queue, which the 100 ms ack-queue limit was tuned on with the transfer in.
- A4: `oneway.rs` matches the design: a monotone deque, buckets of 250 ms, 256 entries reserved once, a shared forward minimum, a receipts-only reverse minimum, a 3-slot ring, refusal of backwards stamps and of stamps more than IO_TIMEOUT above the minimum, and `reset` on Path and Resume.
- A5: credit is built as designed:
  - `on_receipt` takes `at_us`;
  - in one-way mode the ack samples are forward queues;
  - the window's time adds min(least of the newest three reverse queues, 1 s);
  - the frame and byte maximums, `fits` and the JPEG window are unchanged.
- A6: QoS is built as designed: the forward queue feeds `history`, `delay_ms` and `raw`; RTT still feeds the base RTT, the short path and the fast start; the witness is the forward ack queue; `receipt_rate` uses the viewer-clock time and the forward queue.
  - The added floor gap (deviation 2) keeps the one-way delay equal to what the round trip hid under the 10 ms floor. I checked the arithmetic.
  - Behaviour without arrival times is unchanged: RTT samples are now stored unfloored, but `base_rtt` re-applies the floor and `history`/`last_rtt` still use the floored value.
- A7: both Stats fields go only to a viewer whose ledger has one-way state, which exists only when both ends listed `arrival_time`. They also appear in the trace, in `ViewerStats` (the FFI serialises it directly), in the Dart model and in a panel row, with en and zh strings.
- B8: the keyframe slot stores (reason, seq). `discarding()` is false for User, follows `wait_key` for Backlog, and is true for Gap, DecoderError and Stall. The Windows runner drops frames while it awaits a key and asks with Gap, which supports deviation 6.
- B9: `last_keyframe`, `skip_to_keyframe` and `skipping` work as designed; the skip clears when an IDR is booked or after 2 s. B-send drops predicted heads before booking, so seq stays contiguous, and counts them in `dropped_frames`. Rooms are unaffected because `outgoing` belongs to each session. impl.summary:
Receipt-driven rate control (D stage 1) on top of perf2/viewer-feedback (7912cf3). The worktree is at /Users/lb7666/rust_pro/pb-mapper/.claude/worktrees/wf_352d1379-280-47, detached at 41272e3; the branch is free.

Commit A (1905d79), the before build with no host change: crates/pb-mapper-desktop/src/slow_link.rs
- The Interval parser reads rate_fps, standing_ms, cuts and rebase_ms.
- The bandwidth runner becomes a general link_limit runner. Per case it reports lowest pace, pace and received fps over the last 5 s, ack-queue p95/peak/mean, sent over link and recovery time.
- New cases: moderate_limit_keeps_60, sudden_drop, added_route_delay, recurring_stalls_cut.
- lan_rtt now runs 30 s and reports when bpf reaches its max. fixed_wan reports when the pace reaches the ceiling. isolated_stall asserts no receipt cut.

Commit B (99d114d), the behaviour:
- qos/receipt_rate.rs: the shadow estimator now decides. on_receipt returns a Verdict (None, Hold, Cut(bps) or Rebased).
  - Congested means standing > 40 ms, or > 10 ms while a clamped window blocked a unit; stalls that recur also count.
  - Hold: max(rtt+standing, 100 ms), and while used > 1.1 × target, for at most 1 s. A draining queue holds.
  - Two cuts that left the queue within 1.1× rebase onto a receipt-local level, which tracks the minimum between rebases.
  - No busy rate means no cut.
  - Cut target: min(0.85 × busy, 0.9 × used), or 0.85 × used for recurring stalls.
  - raise() runs on the tick: 15%/s, or 4%/s within 0.9 × capacity, plus 100 kbit/s per second, applied in steps of at least 5%, only while used is 0.5 to 1.3 × expected. Capacity clears above 1.2×.
  - Recovery accelerator: 50%/s toward 0.9 × the pre-congestion rate, after 500 ms with the queue under 10 ms.
  - owns(): during an episode, or within 2 s of a cut or rebase. clamp_rate() returns the busy rate during an episode.
  - No allocation per receipt.
- qos.rs:
  - cut_to(): bpf first, down to the preset cut floor. Below it, rate_fps from the delivery rate, down to min_fps; below that, bpf down to the floor. Quality's cut floor is bpf_start/2. raise_to() lifts the pace cap first.
  - pace() is clamped by rate_fps. control_fps gets an owned arm that holds fps below SEVERE_DELAY (600 ms).
  - Rebase offset (capped at 150 ms) applies to the probe delay. It clears when the probe base reaches it, when probes show the route gone, and on path change, resume, preset change and use_one_way.
  - FAST_START_RTT removed: Balanced H.264/H.265 goes to the ceiling at the first untainted probe on any path.
  - close_window skips step_bpf when receipts came in the window. Resets per the brief.
  - adapt() holds a change for 1 s against a Steady overwrite.
- qos/sim.rs (new, test-only): a deterministic closed loop of Qos, CreditLedger, a FIFO bottleneck and a receipting viewer, with 12 cases:
  - per-frame, lagging-VBV, per-second and still encoders;
  - 3 and 1 Mbit/s drops and the lift;
  - an isolated stall and recurring stalls;
  - a longer route (one-way and RTT);
  - reverse-only delay;
  - 4× IDRs near capacity;
  - Quality's cut order.
- credit.rs: window() takes clamp (the episode's busy rate, applied at once). set_rebase() adds the offset to the window time and takes it off the ack queue.
- session.rs: a blocked AtomicBool, set in admissible() when a clamped window refuses a unit with no IDR in flight, and taken by Received. update_qos passes the rebase to the ledger after releasing the qos lock. Path handling goes through update_qos.
- session/sender.rs: the trace gains rate_fps, rebase_ms, cuts and episode; would_cut is removed.
- Tests: receipt_rate unit tests, new qos tests (pace cap and raise order, Quality order, probe ownership, rebase offset, 3 s window skip, adaptation hold), a credit test and a session test. The bandwidth case is renamed bandwidth_limit_cuts_bits_per_frame_then_recovers: it now asserts floor reached, pace ≥ 40 and received ≥ 35 instead of lowest_pace ≤ 15. isolated_stall also asserts no encoder bitrate fall.

Commit C (41272e3):
- docs/remote-desktop.md: pipeline rule 3, send credit, QoS, constants, diagnostics and a measurement note.
- docs/architecture.md.
- DECISIONS.md D5 deviation entry and CONTRACT-perf R13 note, citing the owner's directive.

impl.deviations:
1. Rebase level: kept as the brief's receipt-local level, which tracks the minimum between rebases on top of the probe base. A 10 s windowed own-minimum (the R8 research's) absorbed a queue present from the first receipt; the stage 0 test exposed it.
2. The credit ledger also reads the rebase (it adds to the window time and comes off the ack queue). This goes beyond the brief. In RTT mode the sim showed the ack-queue clamp throttling a longer route to about 43 fps after the rebase. The brief's intent is one shared baseline.
3. Recovery accelerator re-arms once a raise passes 1.2 × capacity after a climb was cut short. Without it the climb was spent probing the limit itself, and the sim took about 7 s to reach 80% after the lift. With it the slow-link suite measured 4 s.
4. Recurring stalls:
   - They trigger a cut, as in R8.
   - Bounded: two stall cuts that leave the stalled share within 1.1× excuse stalls until they stop recurring.
   - A gap counts as a stall only if its first receipt waited through half of it, so a still picture's idle gaps never count.
   - The burst rule also covers a drain: after a gap, each receipt with less delay than the one before.
5. A cut to within 5% of the rate already asked for only holds, and does not count toward a rebase. The sim showed a lagging encoder otherwise getting a false rebase.
6. Choices where the brief left a detail open:
   - The raise gate also requires used ≤ 1.3 × expected (from R8). Without it a per-second encoder at the nominal model would be raised.
   - "Rebase not growing" means no rebase in the last 1 s.
   - Ownership also requires fresh receipts.
   - resume also clears the receipts' rebase level, since the one-way minima restart.
   - Adaptation's single owner is a 1 s hold against Steady.
   - The FAST_START removal skips JPEG.
7. Trace: would_cut is replaced by cuts, and episode is added.
8. Tests:
   - moderate_limit_keeps_60 also asserts received fps ≥ 55 over the last 5 s. The before build held pace 60 but delivered only 38 fps.
   - The bandwidth case is renamed, and its pace assertion replaced as in R8.
   - Commit A was amended once with this before the before runs.
9. Not done:
   - The `video_bench --rate-steps` option does not exist. It is Windows-only, outside the files list, and cannot be compiled here; the device measurement needs it added first.
   - No new macOS VideoToolbox step test: the brief gives that to mac-vt-rate-control.
10. Measured costs:
   - Bandwidth limit: bitrate back to 80% in 4 s in all 5 runs, against 1–2 s before. No run took 5 s.
   - Its ack-queue p95 is 720–724 ms against 211–260 ms, because faster raises reach 8 Mbit/s before the limit starts. The queue over the last 5 s fell to 5–12 ms from 128–184 ms.
   - The per-second-encoder variant recovered in 4, 4, 5, 5 and 6 s.

**1 Mbit/s limit (8 s after 6 s unlimited)**

impl.device_only:
- Encoder response to faster, more frequent bitrate cuts. The MFT encoders on NVIDIA, AMD and Intel GPUs need a new Windows-only `video_bench --rate-steps 8,2,8` option, which does not exist yet. VideoToolbox's response belongs to mac-vt-rate-control. The synthetic encoder here follows a new bitrate on the next frame.
- Real Wi-Fi, cellular and relay traces: how often false cuts happen, read from `standing_ms`, `busy_bps`, `cuts`, `episode` and `rebase_ms` against `ack_queue_ms`, with and without arrival times.
- Subjective judgement of about 50 fps at Balanced's floor versus about 10 fps at a higher bpf, per preset.
- CI only:
  - Windows host and helper build and tests (rust-windows-desktop); the change is platform-neutral and touches no Windows code.
  - rust-macos-desktop.
  - nat-traversal.yml on Linux with sudo.
- Mac hosts shed bandwidth through the fps cap only once their sessions start at the Timestamp model (mac-vt-rate-control). At the Nominal model only bpf cuts shed bandwidth: the per-second slow-link variant still fills the link.

findings.issue: Raises are allowed only while used is at most 1.3 × expected (RAISE_USED_MAX). close_window also skips step_bpf in any 3 s window that had receipts. Together they pin a session at the cut floor whenever the encoder spends more than 1.3 × expected, even after the queue is gone. The pace cap (rate_fps) is pinned too. An encoder at its content floor spends that much, and the repo documents one (MEASURED_CONTENT_FLOOR: NVIDIA's MFT at about 60 kbit per 1080p frame, against Balanced's floor of 16.7 kbit). A per-second encoder at the nominal model with rate_fps = 46 of 60 is another case: 60/46 is 1.304, and the latch needs a pace of 45 or less. Before this PR, step_bpf raised bits per frame on any moving content, and the probe restored fps. The brief's gate (item 4) is only used ≥ 0.5 × expected.
findings.evidence:
Scratch test, reverted afterwards: Balanced settled at 60 on a 20 ms path, then qos.cut_to(30 × 16 667), giving bpf 16 667 and rate_fps 30. Receipts then came every 36 ms, each at the base delay (no queue), with the tick every 250 ms for 20 s.
- 2400-byte frames: rate_fps went 30, then 54, then None, and bpf rose.
- 3000-byte frames (1.44 × the floor's budget): bpf stayed 16 667 and rate_fps Some(30), with pace 30 at every sample to t = 22 s, although no queue existed.
- 4250-byte frames: the same.
Scratch sim, reverted: a per-frame encoder that never makes frames below 3750 bytes, on a 1.2 Mbit/s link from 6 s, lifted at 20 s. From 20 s to 40 s it showed bpf=17000, enc=1020005, standing 0 and cuts 2 at every sample, against 8 Mbit/s before the limit. Code: raise() requires `(RAISE_USED_MIN * expected..=RAISE_USED_MAX * expected).contains(&used)` (receipt_rate.rs:732-734). close_window returns without a step when `receipts.sampled_since(window.started)` (qos.rs:1204-1207).
findings.fix: Do not block raises on used > 1.3 × expected while the queue is clear. Either raise toward the used rate, `next = next.min(used.max(expected))`, which adds no bits on the wire because the encoder already sends them, so bpf follows what the encoder actually spends. Or keep the gate only for the per-second-at-nominal case, by comparing used against the encoder bitrate at the nominal model rather than against expected. Also let close_window step bpf when no receipt raise was possible in the window. Add a sim case with a content-floor encoder (frames ≥ 1.5 × the floor budget), asserting that bpf and rate_fps recover after the limit lifts.

findings.issue: owns() returns true for as long as an episode exists. The new within-5% rule (decide, lines 628-635) answers a congested receipt with Hold. It neither counts a cut nor updates episode.last, so it never reaches a rebase. When the encoder spends more than expected, the computed target min(0.85 × busy, 0.9 × used) always comes out within 5% of expected. The episode then never ends, every decision is Hold, and control_fps skips its cut for any delay below 600 ms. The window clamp holds a standing queue at its limit indefinitely. This is the hole the critique's (a) asked to close. The trigger is an encoder at its content floor, or a per-second encoder at the nominal model. In that state cut_to also computes the carried fps from the nominal bpf, not from what the encoder actually sends, so the fps cut that would shed bandwidth never comes.
findings.evidence:
Scratch sim, reverted: Balanced, one-way, 20 ms path, a per-frame encoder whose frames never fall below 3750 bytes, on a 1.2 Mbit/s link from 6 s.
- From 7.0 s to 20 s every half-second sample read: owns=true, episode=true, cuts=2, pace=60.
- standing stayed at 163 ms, and the probe delay at 156 to 179 ms.
- Nothing cut after 7 s: the decisions were Holds (target 1.02 Mbit/s against expected 17000 × 60 = 1.02 Mbit/s).
The recorded per_second_bandwidth_limit runs show the same pattern (docs/benchmarks/2026-11-24-receipt-rate-control/after-1.txt): cuts=2 and pace 50 from t=1 s to t=5 s, with delay_ms 109 to 301 and ack_queue up to 76 ms. The probe cut fps only after the episode ended, at about 6 s. Before this PR, control_fps would cut at a persisted delay of 150 ms or more, giving fps 56 and below until the queue cleared.
findings.fix: Bound ownership in time. Make owns() true only within OWNED_AFTER of the last cut or rebase, or of the episode's start, not for the whole episode. Or treat a within-5% Hold that recurs after its hold expired, with the queue still above QUEUE_HIGH, as a no-effect cut: it then ends ownership or counts toward the rebase rule. Separately, in cut_to, size the carried fps from the encoder's measured bits per frame, max(bpf, used / pace), so the fps cut sheds bandwidth when the encoder cannot go below its floor. Add a sim case asserting that the queue falls below 100 ms within a few seconds for such an encoder.

findings.issue: update_qos reads rebase_offset() under the qos lock and writes it to the ledger after releasing it. Both B-send (tick, write_state) and B-recv (receipts, echoes, path, resume, preset) call update_qos. B-send can read the old offset, then B-recv changes and stores a new one, then B-send stores the stale one. The ledger keeps the wrong offset in ack_queue and in the window's t until the next update_qos. It also adds a credit-lock acquisition to every receipt and probe echo, for a value that changes only on a rebase.
findings.evidence: session.rs:314-324: `let (changed, rebase) = { let mut qos = self.qos.lock(); change(&mut qos); (..., qos.rebase_offset()) }; self.credit.lock().set_rebase(rebase);`. Session::tick (session.rs:338-342) runs on B-send, and Received and ProbeEcho (session.rs:372-404) run on B-recv. Nothing orders the two set_rebase calls.
findings.fix: Write the offset only from the paths that can change it, all on B-recv: on_receipt, on_probe_echo, reset_baseline, resume and set_preset. Write it only when it changed. Or publish it through an AtomicU64 of nanoseconds that the ledger's callers read, so no stale write can land after a newer one.

findings.issue:
On a light picture, the receipts' fps cap (rate_fps) and the floor bits per frame stay in place long after the link is clear.

- Only the tick's raise() can lift the cap (via Qos::raise_to; set_preset is the only other path that clears rate_fps), and raise() requires used >= 0.5 x expected.
- Expected cannot fall below bpf_floor x pace, so a picture that spends less than that never satisfies the gate.
- The cut can also be triggered by a standing queue the host did not cause:
  - busy_bps counts a pair as busy whenever its delay above the baseline is at least its gap, so behind a queue from cross traffic, Wi-Fi bufferbloat or a longer route it reads the host's own app-limited send rate.
  - cut_to(0.85 x that) then lands below floor x pace and sets rate_fps.
  - At the lower pace the gap exceeds the queue, so busy becomes None. The no-busy allowance of a whole frame interval then hides the queue, so the episode ends with one cut and no rebase.
- The probe controller cannot help, because pace = min(probe fps, rate_fps).
- On the base branch, the same delay leaves the pace at 60 (the 50..100 ms arm) and bits per frame unchanged (the 3 s window raises only on dynamic content).
- This contradicts the CHANGELOG's "the frame rate first" and "a route that becomes longer costs at most two cuts" for such content: an animation, a progress indicator, a small video or terminal output.
findings.evidence:
Two temporary cases added to qos/sim.rs and reverted afterwards, run with `cargo test -p pb-mapper-desktop --lib zz_review -- --nocapture`.

(a) Light picture after a limit:
- Sim::new(typical(), 20, true); Rate(500_000) at 6 s; Rate(0) at 14 s; encoder switched to Encoder::Still (300 B a frame) at 10 s.
- From 11 s to 60 s: pace=42, rate_fps=Some(42), bpf=16667, expected=700014, received_kbit=100.
- So the cap stood for 46 s after the link was unlimited.

(b) Light picture behind a 60 ms queue the host did not cause:
- Sim::new(Encoder::Still, 20, one_way) for both RTT and one-way timing; unlimited link; Change::Delay{forward:70, reverse:10} from 8 s to 20 s.
- From s=9: cuts=1, bpf=16667 (from 66667), pace=13, rate_fps=Some(13), received_kbit=31.
- s=60: still pace=13, rate_fps=Some(13), cuts=1, no rebase. That is 40 s after the delay ended, in both modes.

Code involved:
- raise() gate at receipt_rate.rs:732: `(RAISE_USED_MIN * expected..=RAISE_USED_MAX * expected).contains(&used)`.
- qos.rs raise_to() at 696 and set_preset() are the only places rate_fps is cleared.
- busy_bps at receipt_rate.rs:913: `if end.delay.saturating_sub(baseline) < gap { continue; }`.
findings.fix:
Lift the fps cap on a light picture:
- In raise(), when the receipts are fresh, clear (standing < QUEUE_LOW, no hold or episode), and used < RAISE_USED_MIN x expected, lift rate_fps only (via the Some(cap) arm of raise_to), not bits per frame.
- A light picture costs little at full pace, and any queue it builds cuts again within a round trip.
- Alternatively, clear rate_fps in control_fps when the probes do not own the queue and the delay is under 50 ms.

Do not set the cap from a queue the host did not cause:
- In decide(), treat a congested receipt as app-limited when used < RAISE_USED_MIN x expected, or when the busy rate is within about 10% of the host's own send rate over the same pairs.
- In that case, cut bits per frame at most (no rate_fps), or count it toward the no-effect rebase.

Add sim cases for (a) and (b) that assert the pace returns to 60 within a few seconds of the queue or limit ending.

impl.deviations:
1. The record lives in the host-lived `Shared` in host.rs, not in `Room`. A room closes when its last viewer detaches, so a single viewer reconnecting always gets a new room and a record kept in the room would be gone. A restart (display switch, rename, key rotation) builds a new `Shared` and starts without a record.
2. "Ended by transport loss" is implemented as `End::Closed`. The protocol has no goodbye message, so a viewer's deliberate stop is also `End::Closed`. This matches the brief's measurement, which stops the viewer and reconnects. Sessions the host ends (Disconnect, stop, restart, revoke, codec-change Restarting, protocol error, capture end or failure) leave no record.
3. `Qos::new` takes `Option<ClosingRate>`, the whole record, not a bare start value. The preset and 2-minute checks therefore live in qos.rs, where the unit test exercises them.
4. Added an info trace event, `desktop_start_rate_remembered`, for field diagnosis, and documented it.
5. Measurement method:
   - The new case was run alone (filter `slow_link::reconnect`) 5 times before (773c9d7) and 5 times after (fdcd5b6), rather than running the whole suite 5 times; the whole suite ran once after the change.
   - "Peak ack_queue_ms over the first 3 s" is taken from the session's first three once-a-second trace intervals.
   - The case adds a third session, a viewer on a fast link, to measure the cost the brief accepts in its item 3.
6. Limitation: a viewer that reconnects before the host notices its old session ended (up to the 3 s read timeout) joins the room that session is still in and gets no record from it. This is documented, not changed.
7. Not keyed by codec, as the brief specifies. Because of that, a JPEG viewer within the 2 minutes also starts lower and climbs only by the 3 s window's steps; this is documented.

impl.measurements:
Environment: release builds, 12-core Apple M6, 24 GiB, macOS 27.0 (26A425), Rust 1.99.1. Load average at the start of each run: 1.57 to 3.46 before, 1.67 to 2.47 after. Loopback through a real relay and TLS, the slow_link synthetic per-frame encoder (IDR = 4 × the per-frame budget), and a link shaped to 1 Mbit/s each way. Five runs each on 773c9d7 (before) and fdcd5b6 (after); every run passed.

Reconnect over the same 1 Mbit/s link, 3 s after the stop:

| Measure | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Viewer::connect to first presented picture | 302.6 to 310.8 ms | 98.1 to 108.9 ms (median 306.6 → 105.7) |
| First IDR | 33 332 bytes | 8 332 bytes |
| Peak ack_queue_ms, first three intervals | 263 to 266 | 0 |
| Pace in the first three intervals | 60, 48-49, 48-49 | 60, 36, 43 |
| Pace, mean of intervals 2 to 7 | 47.0 to 48.2 | 44.5 to 47.3 |

The lower pace samples after the change are a measured trade-off. The first cut came at the second interval, with bpf at the floor, so it lowered the pace. The cold session, which has no record, averaged 47.3 to 48.5 on both builds.

Cold first session (unchanged on both builds): 298.7 to 306.4 ms to the first picture, a 33 332-byte IDR, ack-queue peak 264 to 266 ms. The first session ended at Balanced's floor (16 667 bpf) in all runs.

Cost of brief item 3: a viewer on the unlimited link, 3 s after the reconnect ended, reached 80% of Balanced's start 1012 to 1014 ms after connecting before (the first trace interval) and 7011 to 7015 ms after.

Raw output and a README are in docs/benchmarks/2026-11-24-reconnect-start-rate/. host_send_bench was not re-run: no per-packet code changed.

findings.issue: A session that only inherited the record, and never measured its own link, writes the record back with a new timestamp. The floor can therefore last well beyond the 2 minutes. Suppose a fast-link viewer connects within 2 min of a slow-link session's end. It starts at the floor and, on a still or light picture, never climbs. When it closes (End::Closed), acceptor.rs:226-230 stores a new record at the floor with `ended = now`, so the next viewer within 2 min also starts at the floor, and so on with no limit. The record then no longer means what the docs say it means: "about the rate that link last carried", applied "within 2 min of that end".
findings.evidence: `Qos::closing_rate` always returns `bpf: self.bpf / self.pixel_scale, ended: now` (qos.rs:644-650). `Session::closing_rate` checks only `End::Closed` (session.rs:294-297), and `serve` overwrites `shared.closing_rate` with that result (acceptor.rs:226-230). A session started from the record stays at the floor on a light picture for three reasons. First, `ReceiptRate::raise` refuses a raise unless `(!light || inputs.capped)`, where `light = used < RAISE_USED_MIN * expected` (receipt_rate.rs:780-797), and `capped` is `rate_fps.is_some()`, which is None for a new session (qos.rs:773). Second, the 3 s window raises only with `dynamic` content (`step_bpf` factor for delays under 150 ms is `dynamic.then_some(..)`, qos.rs:1446-1449). Third, the window is skipped altogether while receipts sample (close_window, qos.rs:1428-1430). The only measurement of a later viewer used the synthetic encoder, which always fills its budget, so it climbed in 7 s. A still desktop does not climb.
findings.fix: Renew the record only when the session's own controller has evidence about its link. In `Qos`, keep `inherited: Option<Instant>`, set in `Qos::new` to `previous.ended` when the record lowered the start, and clear it in `cut_to` and `step_bpf` whenever they lower bits per frame or set `rate_fps` (receipt or delay evidence). Make `closing_rate` return `ended: self.inherited.unwrap_or(now)`, so an unmeasured echo keeps the original expiry. Add a unit test: a session started from a record that closes unchanged after `START_MEMORY` past the original end leaves a record the next session ignores. In remote-desktop.md, say that a still picture does not climb.

findings.issue: The record also applies to a viewer that joins a room that is already streaming. The room's single encoder runs at the minimum of all its viewers' encoder_bps, so a newcomer that starts at the floor pulls the picture of every viewer already watching down to the floor too, until the newcomer's receipts climb (7 s on a clear link with moving content; not at all on a light picture, as in the first finding). Neither the brief's accepted cost (item 3, "a different viewer ... starts lower") nor docs/remote-desktop.md mentions this cost to other viewers.
findings.evidence: `let previous = *self.shared.closing_rate.lock();` is passed to `Session::new_in_room` on the join path (acceptor.rs:315-327) as well as the new-room path. worker/capture.rs:227-228 computes `encoder_bps = encoder_bps.min(slot.shared.targets.encoder_bps...)` over every unpaused slot, and the result is the bitrate handed to the room's encoder (capture.rs:325).
findings.fix: Either pass `None` on the join path, so the record applies only to a session that opens a new room (a lone viewer reconnecting always does, as deviation 1 notes), or document in remote-desktop.md and the CHANGELOG bullet that a viewer joining within 2 min lowers the shared picture for the viewers already watching until it climbs.

findings.issue: The 2-minute age check uses std::time::Instant. On a macOS host that clock is CLOCK_UPTIME_RAW, which stops while the system sleeps. Example: a session ends, the Mac goes to sleep less than 2 min of uptime later, and a viewer connects soon after wake, hours later. That viewer still gets the old record and starts at its floor, although the link that set it may be long gone.
findings.evidence: `now.saturating_duration_since(self.ended) <= START_MEMORY` (qos.rs:310), where `ended` is `Instant::now()` taken in serve (acceptor.rs:228). The Rust 1.99.1 std docs for Instant (local toolchain share/doc/rust/html/std/time/struct.Instant.html) say "Darwin clock_gettime with CLOCK_UPTIME_RAW" and that whether system suspends count is not specified. The host's `Shared`, which holds the record, lives across the relay re-registration that follows a wake.
findings.fix: Also store the wall-clock end (for example `pb_mapper_core::time::unix_millis()` or SystemTime) in ClosingRate, and apply the record only when both the monotonic and the wall-clock age are within START_MEMORY. Alternatively, clear `shared.closing_rate` when the host's relay registration reconnects.

findings.issue: The QoS startup paragraph and the CHANGELOG bullet report only the gains. They leave out a measured cost to the reconnect's frame rate, which appears only in the benchmark README: the reconnect starts at the floor with Balanced's full 60 FPS fast start, so its first receipt cut has no bits per frame left to cut and lowers the pace instead.
findings.evidence: In docs/benchmarks/2026-11-24-reconnect-start-rate, the after runs show start_pace_fps=[60, 36, 43] against [60, 48-49, 48-49] before, and the README's table gives a mean pace over intervals 2-7 of 44.5 to 47.3 FPS after against 47.0 to 48.2 before. The CHANGELOG bullet says only that the reconnect's "first second of pictures then fit the link", and the remote-desktop.md paragraph has no pace figure.
findings.fix: Add one sentence to the remote-desktop.md paragraph and to the CHANGELOG bullet: with bits per frame already at the floor, the reconnect's first cut lowered its pace to 36 FPS in its second interval, and it averaged 44.5 to 47.3 FPS over intervals 2-7 against 47.0 to 48.2 before. Link the same measurements.

reviews.notes:
I reviewed every changed line of perf2/receipt-rate-control..perf2/reconnect-start-rate (1abf353) and the code around it: qos.rs, session.rs, host.rs, acceptor.rs, the three new tests and the slow_link case, plus the docs, CHANGELOG and benchmark files.

What I checked and found correct:
- **End::Closed classification.** It covers the viewer's EOF, I/O errors, HOST_READ_TIMEOUT and a failed B-send. Host Disconnect, stop, restart and revoke call `end_all` before cancelling, so they are Stopped. The codec-change Restarting is Stopped too, and so are protocol errors and capture end or failure. Only a Host dropped without `stop` turns into Closed, and that writes the record into a `Shared` that is being dropped anyway.
- **Locks.** `Session::closing_rate` drops the `ending` guard before it takes `qos`, so there is no lock nesting. The parking_lot guard on `shared.closing_rate` is never held across an await.
- **Ordering.** The record is written before `room.detach` and before the status clears.
- **Clamp and scale.** They commute: a record from the same preset rescales linearly through `Qos::new` and `expect_video_size`.
- **Latch span.** It is rebuilt after bits per frame are set, so the first tick's peak budget is the lowered one.
- **Protocol and CI rules.** Nothing new goes on the wire, ALPN and HELPER_PROTOCOL are untouched, no production unwrap or expect was added, and nothing changes per packet.
- **Other callers.** No Windows-only code calls `Qos::new` or `Session::new_in_room`.
- **Docs.** The doc claim of 15%/s plus 100 kbit/s matches RAISE_PER_S and RAISE_ADD_BPS. The benchmark README's figures match the raw files. remote-desktop.md has no Chinese pair, and docs/README.md is indexed.

I rebuilt and ran the three new tests here (`cargo test -p pb-mapper-desktop --all-features --lib -- closing_rate closed_connection transport_end`): 3 passed. I did not rerun clippy, the full suite or the slow_link measurements. I deleted target/ afterwards and left the worktree clean, detached at 1abf353.

Not raised as findings:
- **Quality's start.** A Quality reconnect can start below its cut_floor at 24 FPS. The brief's own expected effect assumes Quality starts at its floor, so I did not report it.
- **JPEG remark in the docs.** The JPEG path sends fixed-quality-65 stills (native.rs:192 and the platform still.rs files), so bits per frame do not change a JPEG picture. The docs' remark that a JPEG session climbs only by the 3 s window's steps describes a number the viewer never sees; it is misleading but harmless.
- **Reconnect before the host notices.** Deviation 6, a viewer reconnecting before the host's 3 s read timeout, is partly offset already: the old session is still in the room, so the shared encoder takes the minimum over both and runs at the old session's floor until that session times out.

findings.issue: The docs and CHANGELOG overstate how a session started from a record recovers. They say another viewer (or a viewer whose link has recovered) 'climbs as the receipts raise, 15% a second plus 100 kbit/s a second while its link shows no queue', and the CHANGELOG says such a viewer took 7 seconds to reach 80% of the start. That only holds for a picture that fills its budget. Receipts raise bits per frame only when the used rate is at least half the expected rate. A still or light desktop, the most common content, therefore stays at the remembered floor for as long as it stays light: its first IDR and every later IDR (keyframe requests, a viewer joining) are sized at a quarter of Balanced's start. Without the record it would have held the preset's start. The 7 s figure comes from the synthetic encoder, which always spends its whole budget, so this cost of brief item 3 is understated. It also applies to the same viewer reconnecting after its link recovered.
findings.evidence: qos/receipt_rate.rs:780-796: `let light = used.is_some_and(|used| used < RAISE_USED_MIN * expected); ... && (!light || inputs.capped);` (RAISE_USED_MIN = 0.5). Two existing sim tests already pin this: `a_still_picture_never_raises` (sim.rs:864) and `a_light_picture_lifts_the_pace_cap_once_the_link_clears` (sim.rs:946, bpf <= FLOOR + 1 on a clear link). I ran a scratch sim test here, since reverted: Sim::new(Encoder::Still, 20 ms, one_way) with bpf set to Balanced's floor (what a floor record gives), 30 s on a clear link. Output: bpf = 16667 every second for 30 s. With typical() (a moving picture) the same start climbed 19638, 21987, 27238 ... 133333. The CHANGELOG bullet's 'climbs while its link shows no queue: one on a fast link took 7 seconds' and the README's fast-viewer table both come from the slow_link synthetic encoder only.
findings.fix: State the condition in both places. In docs/remote-desktop.md: a session started below its preset's start raises bits per frame only while its picture uses at least half the expected rate, so on a still or light picture it stays at the remembered rate. Qualify the CHANGELOG's 7 s figure as a moving picture. Better, if the trade-off is wanted: let a start the record lowered climb back toward the preset's start on a clear link whatever the picture, so a light picture is not excluded. For example, arm the receipts' recovery toward the preset start's expected rate, cancelled by the first cut. Add a sim case (Encoder::Still, started from a floor record) and re-measure the slow reconnect.

findings.issue: A JPEG session's closing bits per frame is recorded and later lowers the start of an H.264/H.265 session of the same preset, but that value says nothing about what the link carried. Both JPEG backends encode at a fixed quality 65, so bits per frame never size a JPEG frame. A JPEG session's bpf is still stepped down 5-20% per 3 s window whenever its untainted probes see 150 ms or more of delay. On any link that cannot carry ~8 fps of quality-65 stills, the bpf therefore slides to the floor even though nothing shrank. When the JPEG viewer closes, that floor record starts the next H.264/H.265 viewer within 2 min at a quarter of Balanced's start, on a link that may carry far more.
findings.evidence: session.rs:294-297 records any End::Closed session, whatever its codec. qos.rs close_window: `let receipted = self.codec != VideoCodec::Jpeg && ...`, so a JPEG session always takes `step_bpf(max_delay, ...)`, factor 0.95-0.80 at 150 ms or more. sender.rs:469-471: 'Every JPEG picture is independent; only an H.264 or H.265 IDR ... taints probes', so JPEG probes are untainted. platform/windows/still.rs:27 `JpegEncoder::new_with_quality(&mut jpeg, 65)`; platform/macos/still.rs:2 'as a quality-65 JPEG from ImageIO'. The new host test runs only JPEG viewers, so it records exactly this kind of value.
findings.fix: Return None from `Session::closing_rate` (or `Qos::closing_rate`) when `codec == VideoCodec::Jpeg`, and optionally ignore the record in `Qos::new` for a JPEG session, whose bpf drives nothing. Add a case asserting that a closed JPEG session leaves no record. Move the host test's record assertions to an H.264 backend, or keep them on the record set by hand.

findings.issue: The 2-minute window is measured with `Instant`, which on macOS does not advance while the machine sleeps (std uses CLOCK_UPTIME_RAW on Apple targets). Suppose a Mac host records a slow session's end and the machine sleeps within 2 min. The Host and its `Shared` survive the sleep; registration reconnects inside the client. After waking, the record still applies for whatever awake time remained, possibly hours of wall time later, so the next viewer starts at a stale floor. Windows' QPC-based Instant counts sleep, so this is specific to the macOS host the brief targets.
findings.evidence: `ClosingRate { ended: Instant }` and `now.saturating_duration_since(self.ended) <= START_MEMORY` (qos.rs:309-312). acceptor.rs:228 stamps `Instant::now()`. impl.summary:
Built from perf2/wave1 (bdbcd76). The branch is perf2/pointer-cadence and the worktree is detached at e0a9226.

Host (Rust, pb-mapper-desktop):
- worker/cursor.rs:
  - The cursor interval is now `CURSOR_INTERVAL.min(pacer.period()).max(CURSOR_MIN)`: 16 ms at 60 FPS or less, 8.33 ms at 120 FPS. Const asserts relate CURSOR_MIN, SHAPE_LOOK and SHAPE_LATE.
  - A new `ShapeLook` enum (`First { due, late }` or `Late(due)`) schedules the looks. After a move, the first look comes 2 ms later. A first look that is still pending is kept, so moves less than 2 ms apart never put it off; the late look follows the newest move. A pending late look gives way to a new first look.
  - `sample_cursor` handles both the clock and the looks; `read_cursor(now, look)` does the reading. A look reads `backend.cursor()`, and `cursor_shape()` only if the pointer is visible. If `CursorEcho::reshape` reports a new shape for a slot that reads shapes, the look runs the normal per-slot sampling and restarts `cursor_due`. Otherwise it reports nothing.
  - Any reading that finds a new shape drops the look still pending.
- worker.rs: Engine gains `shape_due: Option<ShapeLook>`, and `deadline()` includes it.
- worker/control.rs: after a Move is injected, a look is set when the slot reads shapes and `self.cursor_shapes` is true.
- Doc comments updated in backend.rs (`Backend::cursor_shape`), platform/mod.rs and platform/windows/cursor.rs (comment only, no code change).
- worker/tests.rs: the fake backend records cursor-read times. Four new stepped-clock tests:
  - a shape set 1 ms after a move is reported at exactly move + 2 ms, and one set at 5 ms is reported at move + 8 ms; the next sample comes 16 ms after the look;
  - an unchanged shape adds no report and is read only at +2 ms and at the last move + 8 ms;
  - a session without cursor_shapes, or a viewer that is not controlling, adds no cursor or shape reads;
  - the pointer is sampled every period at pace 120 and every 16 ms at 60 and 30.
- examples/host_send_bench.rs: the bench backend now reads shapes (an arrow on the left half, a hand on the right). Its pointer is shown only from the new cases on, so the earlier cases behave as before. New cases: `shape` (from a move until the view names the new shape) and `host_pointer` at pace 60 and 120 (from the host's own pointer moving until a watching viewer sees it).

Viewer (Dart):
- remote_cursor_layer.dart: `RemoteCursorLayer` is now a StatefulWidget. It keeps a derived `ValueNotifier<RemoteCursorPaint?>` recomputed from the viewport, `cursorChanges`, the pointer and the pointer's geometry. It notifies only when the paint changes (null to null never does). `RemoteCursorPainter` now takes that ValueListenable.
- desktop_store.dart:
  - `_flushMove` reads the view leaf each time the 4 ms move gate closes, after any pending move is sent.
  - `_acceptView` asks for a frame whenever a read finds the peer pointers changed, the timer's read included; it still asks after an in-frame cursor or shape change.
- Tests (each fails without the change, checked):

- ui/tool/hover_frames.dart: a new measurement tool that runs in the real macOS runner.

findings.issue: The newest move can lose the look it is owed, which is the R4 feature itself. (a) Any reading that finds a new shape sets `self.shape_due = None`, even when the shape answers an earlier move. With a slow app (the case the +8 ms look exists for), the +2 ms look after move B finds the answer to move A and drops B's late look. B's own new shape then waits for the 16 ms clock. (b) `ShapeLook::after_move` (line 52-60) keeps a pending `First` even when its `due` has already passed. A move injected in the second lane drain after a capture call longer than 2 ms keeps A's overdue due. That look runs in the same iterate, at B+0, so B gets no +2 ms look. The brief says a new move restarts the 2 ms look. The deviation's reason ('the app already answered') assumes the shape found answers the newest move, which these cases show is not always true.
findings.evidence: Temporary stepped-clock probe, since reverted, using the PR's shape_session harness. Moves at +0 and +4. The app answers the first at +5 with an I-beam, which the look at +6 reports, and the second at +9 with a hand. The hand was reported at +22 ms, by the regular sample (cursor_due = 6 + 16). With line 142 (`self.shape_due = None;`) commented out, the same probe reported it at +12 ms, the late look 8 ms after the second move. Case (b) follows from the code: `Some(Self::First { due, .. }) => Self::First { due, late }` ignores whether `due < now`, and `sample_cursor` then consumes it at once with `look.next(now)` giving `Late(now + 8)`.
findings.fix: Drop only what the look owes moves already answered. The simplest option is to remove `self.shape_due = None` from the reshape branch: an extra late look costs one cheap read and reports nothing if the shape is unchanged. Alternatively, drop it only when the reading was the late look of the newest move. In `after_move`, keep the pending First only while `due > now` (`Some(Self::First { due, .. }) if due > now`), and otherwise start a new `First { due: now + SHAPE_LOOK, late }`. Add the probe scenario as a test. Update the CHANGELOG phrase 'and once more 8 ms after' and the docs line 'a reading that finds a new shape drops the look still owed'.

findings.issue: RemoteCursorPainter now paints a value cached when a listener last fired (`_paint.value`) instead of computing it at paint time. RemoteViewport defers its notifications for changes made during layout (`_changed()` posts them to after the frame when the phase is persistentCallbacks). RemoteSurface's LayoutBuilder calls `viewport.layout(...)` in exactly that phase, as does `touch_viewer.dart` with `_viewport.layout`. So in the frame that relays out the stage (a window resize, a rotation, the soft keyboard, first mount), the layer repaints because its size changed, but with the old position. The picture moves in that frame and the painted cursor follows one frame later. The base computed `cursor()` inside `paint()` and drew both in the same frame. This affects every painted cursor: watchers, painted shapes and touch viewers.
findings.evidence: Temporary widget probe, since deleted: a LayoutBuilder that calls `h.viewport.layout(constraints.biggest)` around `RemoteCursorLayer`, with the cursor at (0.5, 0.5), resized from 800x600 to 400x300 within one `tester.pump()`, with a debugPrint in `paint`. On the branch the resize frame painted the arrow at Offset(400.0, 300.0) while `viewport.toLocal` gave Offset(200.0, 150.0); the new position was drawn only in the following frame. With the base perf2/wave1 remote_cursor_layer.dart under the same probe, the resize frame painted Offset(200.0, 150.0). (The `paints` matcher cannot show this, because it repaints with current state when it is checked.)
findings.fix: Keep the derived ValueNotifier only as the repaint trigger, and compute what to paint inside paint(). For example, `RemoteCursorPainter(cursor: _paintNow, repaint: _paint)`, with `final RemoteCursorPaint? Function() cursor` and `super(repaint: repaint)`, or have paint() call `_paintNow()`. Hovers that change nothing still notify nothing, so they schedule no frame, and a relayout paints current values. Add a widget test that checks the painted position in the relayout frame, for example by recording what paint() drew rather than using the `paints` matcher.

findings.issue: `no_look_without_a_controller_that_reads_shapes` does not test the guard it names. In its (shapes=true, control=false) case the move is never injected (`inputs() == 0`), so nothing could schedule a look. A single-viewer harness can never separate `slot.cursor_shapes` from `self.cursor_shapes`. Nothing covers the brief's case of a controller that does not read shapes beside a watcher that does, where `self.cursor_shapes` is true.
findings.evidence: Changing control.rs:400 from `if slot.cursor_shapes && self.cursor_shapes {` to `if self.cursor_shapes {` (temporarily, then reverted) left `cargo test -p pb-mapper-desktop --all-features --lib -- worker::tests` at 36 passed, 0 failed. The implementer also reports that this test passes with or without the change.
findings.fix: Use the multi-viewer harness (the one with `join(limits)`). A controlling slot with `cursor_shapes: false` and a joined watcher with `cursor_shapes: true`, the controller moves, and the test asserts no cursor or shape read before the next sample. Keep the session-wide case, and drop or rename the non-controlling case, which only shows that an uninjected move schedules nothing.

Checked and found sound:

findings.issue: Any reading that finds a new shape sets `self.shape_due = None`, including a regular clock sample. That sample can drop the look a newer move left before the look has run. If a slow app answers an earlier move just after a newer move, the sample sees that shape and cancels both of the newer move's looks (+2 ms and +8 ms). The shape the newer move brings then waits for the next sample, up to 16 ms. The brief keeps one more look at +8 ms in every case; the implementer's deviation was meant only to skip a second look for an app that already answered.
findings.evidence: I added a temporary stepped-clock probe in worker/tests.rs, ran it, then reverted it. Setup: shape_session(true, true); move at +10 ms; its 2 ms look finds nothing; second move at +15 ms; hand set at +15.5 ms; the regular sample at +16 ms reports the hand and clears shape_due; I-beam set at +16.5 ms. Output: "ibeam set at +1.5ms after the newest move, seen at +17ms". The look owed at +17 ms (newest move + 2 ms) never ran, so the I-beam came at the next sample (+32 ms).
findings.fix: Drop a pending look only once the app has had SHAPE_LOOK to answer the newest move. Keep the newest move's instant in ShapeLook (for First it is `late - SHAPE_LATE`), and in read_cursor clear shape_due only when `now >= newest_move + SHAPE_LOOK`; otherwise keep it. Add the scenario above as a stepped-clock test.

findings.issue: `no_look_without_a_controller_that_reads_shapes` does not test the guard in control.rs. A watcher's move is never injected, and a session without cursor_shapes is stopped by the separate `self.cursor_shapes` check in sample_cursor. Removing the whole guard (`slot.cursor_shapes && self.cursor_shapes`) still passes every worker test. The untested case is a room where the controller does not read shapes but a watcher does. There, every move by the controller would cost a pointer read and a shape read at +2 ms and +8 ms. The brief says a look follows only a move from a slot that negotiated cursor_shapes.
findings.evidence: Mutation: in worker/control.rs I replaced `if slot.cursor_shapes && self.cursor_shapes {` with `if true {`. Then `cargo test -p pb-mapper-desktop --all-features --lib -- worker::tests` printed "test result: ok. 36 passed; 0 failed". The implementer's report agrees that this test passes either way.
findings.fix: Add a two-viewer case: a controller attached with cursor_shapes false plus a watcher with cursor_shapes true. Inject a move and run 15 ms. Assert cursor_reads_after(moved) is empty and shape_reads is unchanged. That case fails once the `slot.cursor_shapes` half of the guard is removed.

findings.issue: The CHANGELOG bullet and the public trait docs say the host looks at the shape 2 ms and 8 ms after a move, with no conditions. The code skips the 8 ms look once any reading finds a new shape. It also keeps an earlier pending first look, so a move less than 2 ms after another gets its first look sooner than 2 ms after it. The trait docs are `Backend::cursor_shape` in backend.rs, an SDK-facing doc, and `CursorSource::shape` in platform/mod.rs. docs/remote-desktop.md describes the rule correctly.
findings.evidence: CHANGELOG.md:7 says "looks at the pointer's shape 2 ms after it moves the pointer for you, and once more 8 ms after". backend.rs:175-178 says "2 ms and 8 ms after it applied a move from a controller that reads shapes". The code: `ShapeLook::after_move` keeps `First { due, .. }`, and read_cursor sets `self.shape_due = None` on any reshape.
findings.fix: Use the remote-desktop.md wording in all three places, for example: "about 2 ms after a move from a controller that reads shapes, and, while no new shape has been found, once more 8 ms after the last move".

name: mac-viewer-layer
title: macOS viewer: present each decoded 420v picture on a native Core Animation layer from the decoder thread, skipping VideoToolbox's BGRA pass and Flutter's frame

commits: 7f4c7cf Present Mac viewer pictures on a native layer from the decoder thread
4f25d81 Show the Mac layer presenter in an AppKitView and grey it natively
4e9f32e Document the Mac layer presenter and record its measurements
4aa9f72 Keep the keyboard focus off the Mac picture's platform view
aa40f26 Say which build the last layer run used
impl.summary:
Branch perf2/mac-viewer-layer is built on perf2/wave1 (bdbcd76) and holds 5 commits. The worktree is clean and detached, and the build output (target, ui/build, ui/macos/Pods, ui/macos/Flutter/ephemeral) is deleted. The new macOS path works end to end in the real app: receipts flowed, the platform view hosted the layer, and in replays decode was about 2.5–3x faster. But every replay ran with the screen locked and the display asleep, so nothing on screen was checked (time to glass, colours, grey still, pointer, clicks).

Changes, file by file:

- **ui/darwin/DesktopVideo.swift** (runner shared by the macOS and iOS apps):
  - `create` takes `presenter` ('layer' is macOS only; 'texture' or no value gives a texture; anything else is an error). Layer viewers get ids from the plugin's own counter starting at 1, with no FlutterTexture registered. The texture limit and the instance check are unchanged.
  - Layer mode decodes to 420v (IOSurface, Metal-compatible). At configure, `forLayer` always rebuilds the format description with sRGB transfer, BT.709 primaries and the stream's matrix (709 when missing). The first decoded picture is checked for the sRGB tag; if it lacks it, `tagSrgb` tags every picture and also removes the CGColorSpace attachment.
  - `LayerPresenter`: a container layer holding the content layer and two hidden grey layers. All layers use a delegate that turns off animations. The decoder thread commits `content.contents = IOSurface` in its own explicit transaction and keeps the last 3 pictures out of VideoToolbox's pool.
  - `present()` runs the old copyPixelBuffer receipt logic after each commit (revision check, presented += 1, `timings.present` from decode end to commit end) and calls `library.presented` outside the lock.
  - `DesktopVideoView`: a layer-backed NSView whose own layer hosts the presenter's container. It accepts the first mouse, never becomes first responder, cannot move the window, adds no cursor rects, and swallows cursorUpdate through a tracking area.
  - The plugin is the platform-view factory for `pb_mapper/desktop_video_view` (standard message codec) and logs each view it makes. New channel method `grey`.
  - `RefreshLink`: on macOS 14+ an NSView display link, before that a CVDisplayLink for counting only. It asks a variable-refresh display for its fastest rate and, while timings are on, counts commits beyond the first in a refresh as `dropped`. Pause and resume reach the main thread tagged with the consumer, so a word from a detached source changes nothing.
  - Snapshots use the picture committed last. iOS keeps the texture path unchanged.
- **ui/lib/src/ffi/desktop_video.dart**: `DesktopVideoTexture` gains `platformViewType` and `grey(bool)`. `desktopVideoPresenter` is 'layer' on macOS unless built with `--dart-define=presenter=texture`. `presenter` is sent in `create` on macOS only.
- **ui/lib/src/state/desktop_models.dart**: `DesktopPicture` gains `platformViewType`.
- **ui/lib/src/state/desktop_store.dart**: the picture carries the view type; new `greyPicture(bool)`.
- **ui/lib/src/pages/remote/viewer/viewer_stage.dart**: when the picture has a view type, the stage builds an `AppKitView` (keyed by id, `{'textureId': id}`, opaque to hits) inside `ExcludeFocus`; otherwise the Texture as before. New `greyPicture` parameter; `ViewerStage.of` passes the store's.
- **ui/lib/src/pages/remote/viewer/viewer_overlays.dart**: `GreyStill` is now stateful. For a runner-presented picture it calls `greyPicture(true/false)` when the grey state changes or the stage goes, and builds no BackdropFilter.
- **ui/test/fake_desktop_api.dart**: the fake texture's view type is null by default and `grey` only records calls; `FakeTextures.platformViewType` makes textures with one.
- **New tests**:
  - viewer_chrome_test: AppKitView in place of Texture, with the right creation parameters sent on the platform_views channel; it cannot take keyboard focus; grey turns on during reconnect and off when live or when the stage goes; no BackdropFilter. The existing test still covers the Texture path with the fake.
  - desktop_store_test: the view type reaches the picture, `greyPicture` reaches only a presenting texture, and nothing after disconnect.
- **ui/tool/desktop_viewer_acceptance.dart**: the report records `presenter`.
- **Docs**:
  - docs/remote-desktop.md: quality-panel Mac row, how to read the rates, the app's video path (the receipt now means committed to the WindowServer), the macOS decoder section rewritten around the two presenters, and the test-status rows.
  - docs/architecture.md, scripts/test/desktop-ui-acceptance.md (how to A/B the presenters), docs/README.md index, and a CHANGELOG bullet.
  - New record docs/benchmarks/2026-11-24-mac-viewer-layer/: README, scripts, harnesses with raw output, summary.jsonl, samples.json, runs-load.txt.
impl.deviations:
- **Design 5, the view**: it is layer-backed and adds the presenter's container as a sublayer, instead of a layer-hosting view whose layer is the container. With layer-hosting, removing an old view from its superview would also remove a layer that a newer view had taken over. viewcheck.swift showed the layer-backed version works: the container followed resizes and stayed in place when the first view was removed. `layerUsesCoreImageFilters` is not set, because nothing uses CIFilters.
- **Design 7, grey still**: done with Core Animation compositing filters (a `colorBlendMode` layer over grey, then 50% black), not a CIColorMatrix. Measured offscreen with CARenderer, a CIColorMatrix with GreyStill's coefficients came out up to 57 levels too bright (mid-grey 92 instead of 64), consistent with the matrix being applied in linear light. The compositing filters came within 9 levels of GreyStill's grey (the blend mode weighs luminance 0.3/0.59/0.11 rather than BT.709's), with mid-grey exact.
- **Design 3, colour fallback**: setting the transfer attachment alone does not reach Core Animation. The IOSurface keeps a BT.709 colour space, which Core Animation reads first, so the picture still showed 12 levels lighter. The fallback therefore also removes the CGColorSpace attachment, which measured within 2 levels. The check needs `CVBufferCopyAttachment`, which exists only from macOS 12; before 12 the tag is assumed present.
- **Design 8, display link**: it runs only while a source streams to a view on screen, and only on a variable-refresh display (minimumRefreshInterval < maximumRefreshInterval, so ProMotion and adaptive sync) or while timings are on. A fixed-refresh display with the quality panel closed runs no link. The frame-rate request is kept because the ProMotion check that could remove it was not possible here.
- **Design 12**: GreyStill reaches the texture through the store's `greyPicture`, which `ViewerStage.of` passes in, because the stage takes listenables rather than the store or the texture.
- **Additions not in the brief**:
  - `ExcludeFocus` around the AppKitView: AppKitView adds a Focus node, and if focus traversal reached it, it would take the keys away from the viewer. The test for this fails without the exclusion.
  - `presenter` in the acceptance report.
  - A log line each time the platform view is made.
- **Measurement (c) is partial**: the screen was locked with the display asleep throughout (`CGDisplayIsAsleep` true, loginwindow shield on screen), and screen capture failed here (CGWindowListCreateImage returned blank, ScreenCaptureKit error -3811, `screencapture` refused). So there are no Instruments runs, no os_signposts, no decode-to-glass numbers and no on-screen colour.
- **Analysis window**: about 31 s into every texture run, Flutter's compositor fell to taking 4–8 pictures a second, while layer runs kept committing every picture. Both presenters are therefore compared over the same window, from the end of warm-up to 29 s.

impl.measurements:
All on this Mac (12-core M6, 24 GiB, macOS 27.0 26A425, Rust 1.99.1, Flutter 3.50.1), release builds, G24H2 at 144 Hz. The console was locked and the display asleep throughout. Other agents were building at the same time (1-minute load 2.6–12.3). Full record: docs/benchmarks/2026-11-24-mac-viewer-layer/README.md.

**In-app replays** (desktop_ui_host H.264 clips, view-only, relay over TCP on loopback). Two runs per presenter per case, order reversed in the second round. Medians over warm-up to 29 s; texture first, then layer:

| Case | Decode ms (texture → layer) | Commit ms (layer) | Release to consume ms (texture) | Viewer CPU % (texture → layer) | WindowServer CPU % (texture → layer) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1080p 60 | 2.55, 2.61 → 0.78, 0.88 | 0.24, 0.35 | 3.8, 3.9 | 7.8, 8.2 → 4.4, 4.9 | 2.3, 1.8 → 5.0, 3.6 |
| 1440p 60 | 2.60, 2.52 → 1.29, 1.04 | 0.21–0.52 | 3.7–4.0 | 5.6, 5.5 → 6.5, 4.0 | 1.5–1.7 → 3.0–4.5 |
| 4K 60 | 5.16, 4.84 → 1.94, 1.91 | 0.33–0.42 | 3.8–3.9 | 8.5, 7.5 → 5.4, 5.1 | 1.7–2.6 → 3.2–4.3 |
| 1080p 120 | 2.35, 2.13 → 0.86, 0.84 | 0.35–0.39 | 3.7 | 12.3, 10.5 → 8.5, 9.2 | 2.9–3.1 → 5.9–6.0 |
| 4K 120 | 4.77, 5.05 → 1.78, 1.70 | 0.20–0.28 | 3.5–3.6 | 11.0, 12.7 → 7.8, 6.6 | 2.7–2.9 → 5.0–5.4 |

- The decoder thread's CPU rose by 12–46 ms a second, because the commit now runs on it.
- Viewer plus WindowServer together was lower with the layer in 8 of 10 pairs and higher in 2 (by 1.5 and 3.9 points).
- At 4K 120 the texture path presented 1.1 and 1.9 fewer pictures a second than it decoded; the layer committed every picture. The layer's own dropped count needs the display link, which never fired with the display asleep, so its zeros mean nothing.
- GPU utilisation read 0 almost throughout, as expected with nothing composited to a screen.

**Offscreen (CARenderer harness colourcheck.swift)**:
- 420v tagged sRGB came within 2 levels of today's BGRA on 8 patches; left with the 709 transfer it was up to 12 levels lighter (mid-grey 128 shown as 139).
- An IOSurface as layer contents is drawn the same way up as a CGImage.
- Snapshot conversion: the layer's picture is within 2 levels of the sRGB source; the texture path's BGRA (tagged 709) comes out up to 11 levels lighter.
- Grey still figures are in the deviations.

**viewcheck.swift**: the container follows view resizes and survives the old view's removal; commits from a thread with no run loop work without warnings.
